title.en: Volume 319 Biographies 78: Ouyang Xiu and Sons: Fa, Fei , Liu Chang and Younger Brother: Ban, Son : Fengshi, Zeng Gong and Younger Brother: Zhao
title.raw: 卷三百十九 列傳第七十八 歐陽修子:發 棐 劉敞弟:攽 子:奉世 曾鞏弟:肇 Volume 319 Biographies 78: Ouyang Xiu and Sons: Fa, Fei , Liu Chang and Younger Brother: Ban, Son : Fengshi, Zeng Gong and Younger Brother: Zhao

sentences.zh: 歐陽脩

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu

sentences.zh: 歐陽脩，字永叔，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu, with the style name Yongshu, was a man of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu, styled Yongshu, was a native of Luling.

sentences.zh: 四歲而孤，母鄭，守節自誓，親誨之學，家貧，至以荻畫地學書。

translations.literal: At four years he was orphaned. His mother, of the Zheng clan, vowed to preserve her chastity and personally instructed him in learning. The family was poor, to the point of using reeds to draw on the ground for him to practice writing.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at the age of four. His mother, née Zheng, bound herself to widowhood and taught him herself. The household was so poor that she traced characters on the ground with reeds for him to learn to write.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟過人，讀書輒成誦。

translations.literal: In youth his quick perception surpassed others; whenever he read something he could at once recite it.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was unusually quick-witted: whatever he read, he could recite from memory at once.

sentences.zh: 及冠，嶷然有聲。

translations.literal: When he reached adulthood, he already stood out with a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he came of age, he was already widely known for his promise.

sentences.zh: 宋興且百年，而文章體裁，猶仍五季餘習，鎪刻駢偶，淟涊弗振，士因陋守舊，論卑氣弱。

translations.literal: The Song had risen for nearly a hundred years, yet the forms and styles of writing still followed the remnants of the Five Dynasties—overwrought parallel ornament, turbid and stagnant, unable to stir. Scholars, because of habit, clung to the old; discourse was low and the scholarly air weak.
translations.idiomatic: The Song dynasty had been established for nearly a century, yet literary style still bore the habits of the Five Dynasties—overwrought parallel prose, mired and lifeless, unable to rouse itself. Scholars clung to old ways out of inertia; argument ran shallow and the scholarly temper was weak.

sentences.zh: 蘇舜元、舜欽、柳開、穆修輩，咸有意作而張之，而力不足。

translations.literal: Su Shunyuan, Su Shunqin, Liu Kai, Mu Xiu and others all had the intent to create [new writing] and expand it, but their strength was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shunyuan, Su Shunqin, Liu Kai, Mu Xiu, and others all wished to revive and champion a better tradition, but lacked the strength to do so.

sentences.zh: 修游隨，得唐韓愈遺稿於廢書簏中，讀而心慕焉。

translations.literal: Xiu, traveling in Suizhou, obtained Tang Han Yu's surviving drafts from among discarded books, read them, and in his heart admired them.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling in Suizhou, he found Han Yu's surviving manuscripts in a pile of discarded books, read them, and came to admire them deeply.

sentences.zh: 苦志探賾，至忘寢食，必欲並轡絕馳而追與之並。

translations.literal: With bitter resolve he probed their profundities, to the point of forgetting sleep and food, determined that he must drive abreast and at full gallop to catch and run alongside [Han Yu].
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into probing their depths, forgetting food and sleep, determined to run neck and neck with Han Yu and catch up to him.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，試南宮第一，擢甲科，調西京推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, placed first in the Southern Palace examination, was selected for the top grade, and was appointed Vice Magistrate of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, ranked first in the palace examination, was placed in the top grade, and was appointed Vice Magistrate of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 始從尹洙遊，爲古文，議論當世事，迭相師友，與梅堯臣遊，爲歌詩相倡和，遂以文章名冠天下。

translations.literal: He first associated with Yin Zhu, wrote ancient-style prose, discussed affairs of the age, and in turn became each other's teacher and friend. He associated with Mei Yaochen, and they made songs and poems calling and responding to each other; thus with his writing he came to be foremost in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He first befriended Yin Zhu, wrote in the ancient prose style, and debated the affairs of the day, each serving as the other's teacher and friend. He also befriended Mei Yaochen, and together they composed poetry in mutual response. Thus his literary fame came to crown the empire.

sentences.zh: 入朝，為館閣校勘。

translations.literal: Upon entering court, he served as collator in the Hall of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: After entering court, he served as collator in the Hall of Literature.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹以言事貶，在廷多論救，司諫高若訥獨以為當黜。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan was demoted for speaking on affairs; many at court argued to save him, but Remonstrance Official Gao Ruona alone held that he ought to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan was demoted for remonstrating, many at court spoke up in his defense, but Remonstrance Official Gao Ruona alone held that the demotion was justified.

sentences.zh: 修貽書責之，謂其不復知人間有羞恥事。

translations.literal: Xiu sent him a letter reproaching him, saying that he no longer knew that among men there are matters of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu sent him a letter of rebuke, saying that he no longer knew that human beings are capable of shame.

sentences.zh: 若訥上其書，坐貶夷陵令，稍徙乾德令、武成節度判官。

translations.literal: Ruona submitted his letter [to the throne]; [Xiu] was demoted to magistrate of Yiling, then gradually transferred to magistrate of Qian'e and military commissioner judge of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ruona submitted the letter to the throne, and Xiu was demoted to Magistrate of Yiling, then gradually transferred to Magistrate of Qian'e and Military Commissioner Judge of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 仲淹使陝西，辟掌書記，修笑而辭曰：「昔者之舉，豈以爲己利哉？

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan was sent to Shaanxi and summoned him to serve as chief secretary; Xiu smiled and declined, saying: "That former recommendation—was it made for my private profit?
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhongyan was dispatched to Shaanxi, he invited Xiu to serve as his chief secretary. Xiu smiled and declined, saying, "When you recommended me before, was it for my private gain?

sentences.zh: 同其退不同其進可也。」

translations.literal: To share in withdrawal but not in advancement—that is permissible."
translations.idiomatic: One may share in another's fall from favor, but not necessarily in his rise to power.

sentences.zh: 久之，復校勘，進集賢校理。

translations.literal: After a long while he was restored as collator and promoted to proofreader in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored as collator and promoted to proofreader in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，知諫院。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was again made collator and advanced to collator of the Hall for the Veneration of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was restored as collator and promoted to collator of the Hall for the Veneration of Literature.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗更用大臣，杜衍、富弼、韓琦、范仲淹皆在位，增諫官員，用天下名士，修首在選中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, he was made director of the Remonstrance Bureau. At that time Emperor Renzong was replacing and employing great ministers; Du Yan, Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan were all in office. The remonstrance offices were increased and famous men of the realm were employed—Xiu was foremost among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Qingli era, he was appointed Director of the Remonstrance Bureau. At that time Emperor Renzong was bringing new chief ministers into office—Du Yan, Fu Bi, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan were all in power—and the remonstrance posts were expanded to draw men of renown from across the empire. Xiu headed the list of those chosen.

sentences.zh: 每進見，帝延問執政，咨所宜行。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered audience, the Emperor would prolong the interview and ask the chief ministers, consulting what ought to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was received in audience, the emperor would detain him to question the chief ministers and seek his counsel on what ought to be done.

sentences.zh: 既多所張弛，小人翕翕不便。

translations.literal: After many measures had been loosened or tightened, petty men murmured together that it was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Once many reforms had been enacted, petty men whispered among themselves that the changes were intolerable.

sentences.zh: 修慮善人必不勝，數為帝分別言之。

translations.literal: Xiu, fearing that good men would certainly not prevail, several times spoke to the Emperor to distinguish and explain this for him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that good men would not prevail, Xiu repeatedly explained the matter to the emperor, distinguishing truth from slander.

sentences.zh: 初，范仲淹之貶饒州也，修與尹洙、余靖皆以直仲淹見逐，目之曰「黨人」。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan Zhongyan was demoted to Raozhou, Xiu together with Yin Zhu and Yu Jing had all, because of their forthrightness on Zhongyan's behalf, been driven out, and were labeled "party men."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fan Zhongyan was demoted to Raozhou, Xiu, Yin Zhu, and Yu Jing had all been expelled for speaking up forthrightly on his behalf and were labeled "members of a faction."

sentences.zh: 自是，朋黨之論起，修乃為《朋黨論》以進。

translations.literal: From this time the theory of faction arose, and Xiu thereupon composed the "Discourse on Factions" and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the rhetoric of factionalism took hold, and Xiu composed his "Discourse on Factions" and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「君子以同道爲朋，小人以同利爲朋，此自然之理也。

translations.literal: Its gist said: "Gentlemen unite as factions through shared principle; petty men unite as factions through shared profit—this is the natural order of things.
translations.idiomatic: Its gist ran thus: "Gentlemen form factions through shared principle; petty men form factions through shared profit—this is the natural order of things.

sentences.zh: 臣謂小人無朋，惟君子則有之。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that petty men have no factions; only gentlemen have them.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that petty men have no true factions; only gentlemen do.

sentences.zh: 小人所好者利祿，所貪者財貨，當其同利之時，暫相黨引以爲朋者，僞也。

translations.literal: What petty men love are salary and rank; what they covet are wealth and goods. When they share profit for a time, they temporarily band together and call themselves a faction—but it is false.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men love salary and rank and covet wealth and goods. When their interests align for a moment, they may band together and call themselves a faction, but the bond is false.

sentences.zh: 及其見利而爭先，或利盡而反相賊害，雖兄弟親戚，不能相保，故曰小人無朋。

translations.literal: When they see profit and race to be first, or when profit is exhausted and in turn they harm one another, even brothers and kin cannot protect each other—thus it is said petty men have no factions.
translations.idiomatic: When profit appears they scramble ahead of one another; when profit is exhausted they turn on each other. Even brothers and kin cannot protect one another—hence the saying that petty men have no factions.

sentences.zh: 君子則不然，所守者道義，所行者忠信，所惜者名節。

translations.literal: Gentlemen are not so. What they uphold is moral principle; what they practice is loyalty and trustworthiness; what they cherish is reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen are otherwise. What they uphold is moral principle; what they practice is loyalty and trustworthiness; what they prize is reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 以之修身，則同道而相益，以之事國，則同心而共濟，終始如一，故曰惟君子則有朋。

translations.literal: Using these to cultivate the self, they share the Way and mutually benefit; using these to serve the state, they share one heart and together cross difficulties—consistent from beginning to end. Thus it is said that only gentlemen have factions.
translations.idiomatic: In self-cultivation they share the Way and strengthen one another; in serving the state they share one heart and bear difficulties together—constant from beginning to end. Thus only gentlemen have true factions.

sentences.zh: 紂有臣億萬，惟億萬心，可謂無朋矣，而紂用以亡。

translations.literal: Zhou had ministers by the tens of thousands, yet tens of thousands of hearts—this may be called having no faction—and yet Zhou for this perished.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Shang had ministers by the tens of thousands, yet tens of thousands of hearts—one may say he had no faction—and for that his house perished.

sentences.zh: 武王有臣三千，惟一心，可謂大朋矣，而周用以興。

translations.literal: King Wu had ministers by the thousands, yet one heart—this may be called a great faction—and Zhou for this rose.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu had three thousand ministers, yet one heart—one may call that a great faction—and for that the Zhou rose.

sentences.zh: 蓋君子之朋，雖多而不厭故也。

translations.literal: In general, the factions of gentlemen, though many, are not wearisome for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: In short, the factions of gentlemen, though numerous, are never burdensome for this reason.

sentences.zh: 故為君但當退小人之僞朋，用君子之真朋，則天下治矣。」

translations.literal: Therefore for a ruler one need only dismiss the false factions of petty men and employ the true factions of gentlemen, and the realm will be governed."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a ruler need only dismiss the false factions of petty men and employ the true factions of gentlemen, and the realm will be well governed."

sentences.zh: 修論事切直，人視之如仇，帝獨獎其敢言，面賜五品服，顧侍臣曰：「如歐陽修者，何處得來？」

translations.literal: When Xiu discussed affairs he was cutting and direct; men regarded him as an enemy, yet the Emperor alone rewarded his daring in speech, and in person bestowed fifth-rank court dress, saying to attendant ministers: "Where could one obtain another like Ouyang Xiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's remonstrances were blunt and uncompromising; many treated him as an enemy, yet the emperor alone praised his courage in speaking out, personally bestowing fifth-rank court dress on him and saying to his attendants, "Where does one find another like Ouyang Xiu?"

sentences.zh: 同修起居注，遂知制誥。

translations.literal: Together with [his appointment as] compiler of the Veritable Records, he was then made drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently appointed Compiler of the Veritable Records and then made Drafting Academician.

sentences.zh: 故事，必試而後命，帝知修，詔特除之。

translations.literal: By precedent one had to pass an examination before receiving appointment, but the Emperor knew Xiu and issued an edict specially appointing him.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent an examination was required before appointment, but knowing Xiu's ability, the emperor issued an edict appointing him directly.

sentences.zh: 奉使河東。

translations.literal: He was sent on mission to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched on a mission to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 自西方用兵，議者欲廢麟州以省饋餉。

translations.literal: Since military campaigns had begun in the west, those who discussed policy wished to abolish Lin Prefecture to economize on provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Since the western campaigns had begun, policy advocates proposed abolishing Lin Prefecture to save on supplies.

sentences.zh: 修曰：「麟州，天險，不可廢；

translations.literal: Xiu said: "Lin Prefecture is a natural stronghold and cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "Lin Prefecture is a natural fortress and cannot be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 廢之，則河內郡縣，民皆不安居矣。

translations.literal: If it is abolished, then the people of the interior commanderies and counties will all be unable to dwell in peace.
translations.idiomatic: If it were abandoned, the people of the interior prefectures and counties would no longer live in security.

sentences.zh: 不若分其兵，駐並河內諸堡，緩急得以應援，而平時可省轉輸，於策為便。」

translations.literal: It would be better to divide its troops and station them in the various forts along the Yellow River; in emergency one could respond with aid, while in normal times one could save on transport—a convenient policy.
translations.idiomatic: Better to divide its garrison among the Yellow River forts: in crisis they could respond at once, while in peacetime transport costs would be reduced. That policy would serve.

sentences.zh: 由是州得存。

translations.literal: Because of this the prefecture was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: On this advice the prefecture was preserved.

sentences.zh: 又言：「忻、代、岢嵐多禁地廢田，願令民得耕之，不然，將為敵有。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In Xin, Dai, and Kechan there is much forbidden land and abandoned fields; I wish that the people may be allowed to till them, lest otherwise they fall to the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, "Xin, Dai, and Kechan hold much forbidden and abandoned land. Let the people farm it, or the enemy will seize it."

sentences.zh: 朝廷下其議，久乃行，歲得粟數百萬斛。

translations.literal: The court transmitted his proposal for discussion; only after a long time was it carried out, and each year several million hu of grain were gained.
translations.idiomatic: The court referred his proposal for deliberation; only after a long delay was it enacted, yielding several million hu of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 凡河東賦斂過重民所不堪者，奏罷十數事。

translations.literal: As for all the excessive tax levies in Hedong that the people could not bear, he memorialized to abolish more than ten items.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Hedong's tax levies were so heavy that the people could not endure them, he memorialized to abolish more than ten such impositions.

sentences.zh: 使還，會保州兵亂，以爲龍圖閣直學士、河北都轉運使。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission, it happened that the Baozhou garrison mutinied; he was made Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Grand Transport Commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, the Baozhou garrison mutinied. He was appointed Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Grand Transport Commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝曰：「勿爲久留計，有所欲言，言之。」

translations.literal: On taking leave at the imperial audience, the Emperor said: "Do not plan to stay long; if there is something you wish to say, say it."
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave at court, the emperor said, "Do not plan on a long stay. If you have something to say, say it."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣在諫職得論事，今越職而言，罪也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant, in the remonstrance office, could discuss affairs; now to speak beyond my office is a crime."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In the remonstrance office I was entitled to discuss policy. To speak now beyond my proper duties would be an offense."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「第言之，毋以中外為間。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Simply speak—do not regard inner and outer as a barrier."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Speak freely. Do not let the distinction between court and provinces restrain you."

sentences.zh: 賊平，大將李昭亮、通判馮博文私納婦女，修捕博文繫獄，昭亮懼，立出所納婦。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the great general Li Zhaoliang and Vice Commissioner Feng Bowen privately took women; Xiu arrested Bowen and imprisoned him. Zhaoliang was afraid and at once released the women he had taken.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, the great general Li Zhaoliang and Vice Commissioner Feng Bowen had privately taken women. Xiu arrested Bowen and put him in prison. Zhaoliang, in fear, immediately released the women he had taken.

sentences.zh: 兵之始亂也，招以不死，既而皆殺之，脅從二千人，分隸諸郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the soldiers' mutiny they had been promised that they would not die if they surrendered; afterward they were all killed. The two thousand who had been coerced were distributed among the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the mutiny the rebels had been promised their lives if they surrendered; afterward they were all put to death. The two thousand who had been coerced into joining were distributed among the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 富弼爲宣撫使，恐後生變，將使同日誅之，與修遇於內黃，夜半，屏人告之故。

translations.literal: Fu Bi was Commissioner for Public Tranquillization and, fearing trouble afterward, intended to have them executed on the same day. He met Xiu at Neihuang, and at midnight, sending others away, told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi, serving as Commissioner for Public Tranquillization, feared future trouble and planned to execute them all on the same day. He met Xiu at Neihuang and, at midnight, dismissed attendants and told him his plan.

sentences.zh: 修曰：「禍莫大於殺已降，況脅從乎？

translations.literal: Xiu said: "No calamity is greater than killing those who have already surrendered—how much more those who were coerced!
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "No disaster is greater than killing men who have already surrendered—how much more those who were coerced!

sentences.zh: 既非朝命，脫一郡不從，爲變不細。」

translations.literal: Since this is not an order from the court, if a single prefecture does not comply, the resulting disturbance will not be slight."
translations.idiomatic: This is not an order from court. If even one prefecture refuses to comply, the resulting disturbance will not be slight.

sentences.zh: 弼悟而止。

translations.literal: Fu Bi understood and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi understood and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 方是時，杜衍等相繼以黨議罷去，修慨然上疏曰：「杜衍、韓琦、范仲淹、富弼，天下皆知其有可用之賢，而不聞其有可罷之罪，自古小人讒害忠賢，其說不遠。

translations.literal: At that time Du Yan and others were in succession removed because of faction discourse. Xiu, indignant, submitted a memorial saying: "Du Yan, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi are known throughout the realm as men of talent who may be employed, and one does not hear that they have offenses for which they ought to be dismissed. From antiquity petty men have slandered loyal and worthy men—their methods are not far to seek.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Yan and the others were removed one after another on charges of factionalism. Indignant, Xiu submitted a memorial: "Du Yan, Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, and Fu Bi are known throughout the empire as men of talent fit for service, yet one hears no crimes that would justify their dismissal. From antiquity petty men have slandered the loyal and worthy by familiar means.

sentences.zh: 欲廣陷良善，不過指爲朋黨，欲動搖大臣，必須誣以顓權，其故何也？

translations.literal: If one wishes broadly to entrap the good and worthy, nothing surpasses calling them a faction; if one wishes to shake great ministers, one must falsely accuse them of monopolizing power—what is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: To entrap the good and worthy broadly, nothing works better than calling them a faction; to shake great ministers, one must falsely accuse them of monopolizing authority. Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 去一善人，而眾善人尚在，則未爲小人之利；

translations.literal: Remove one good man and the host of good men remain—then it is not yet to the petty men's profit.
translations.idiomatic: Remove one good man and the rest remain—the petty men's gain is still small.

sentences.zh: 欲盡去之，則善人少過，難爲一一求瑕，唯指以爲黨，則可一時盡逐，至如自古大臣，已被主知而蒙信任，則難以他事動搖，惟有顓權是上之所惡，必須此說，方可傾之。

translations.literal: If one wishes to remove them all, then good men have few faults and it is hard to seek blemishes one by one; only by calling them a faction can one drive them all out at once. As for great ministers of antiquity who were already known to the ruler and enjoyed trust, it was hard to move them by other matters; only "monopolizing power" is what the ruler detests—one must use this saying before one can overturn them.
translations.idiomatic: To remove them all, good men offer few faults and are hard to indict one by one. Only by calling them a faction can they be driven out at once. As for great ministers already known to the ruler and enjoying his trust, other charges seldom avail; only the accusation of monopolizing power, which rulers detest, can bring them down.

sentences.zh: 正士在朝，群邪所忌，謀臣不用，敵國之福也。

translations.literal: When upright gentlemen are at court, the host of evil men resent them; when strategists are not employed, it is the enemy state's good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When upright gentlemen serve at court, the wicked resent them; when able strategists go unused, it is the enemy's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 今此四人一旦罷去，而使群邪相賀於內，四夷相賀於外，臣爲朝廷惜之。」

translations.literal: Now these four men have been dismissed all at once, making the evil faction congratulate one another within and the four barbarians congratulate one another without—I grieve for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Now these four have been dismissed at once, letting the wicked congratulate one another within and the barbarians without. I grieve for the court."

sentences.zh: 於是邪黨益忌修，因其孤甥張氏獄傅致以罪，左遷知制誥、知滁州。

translations.literal: Thereupon the evil faction resented Xiu all the more and, through the case of his orphaned nephew's wife Zhang, fabricated charges and attached guilt to him; he was demoted to Drafting Academician and made prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The wicked faction then resented him all the more. Through the case of his orphaned nephew's wife, the Zhang clan, they fabricated charges against him. He was demoted to Drafting Academician and appointed Prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 居二年，徙揚州、潁州。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to Yangzhou and Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was transferred to Yangzhou and Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 復學士，留守南京，以母憂去。

translations.literal: He was again made Academician and put in charge as administrative coordinator of Nanjing, then left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to his academician title and appointed administrative coordinator of Nanjing, then left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服除，召判流內銓，時在外十二年矣。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned to serve as judge of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs; by then he had been outside [the capital] for twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was summoned to serve as judge of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs. By then he had been away from the capital for twelve years.

sentences.zh: 帝見其髮白，問勞甚至。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing that his hair was white, inquired after him with extreme kindness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw that his hair had turned white and questioned him with exceptional warmth.

sentences.zh: 小人畏修復用，有詐爲修奏，乞澄汰內侍爲奸利者。

translations.literal: Petty men feared Xiu's restoration to office; someone forged a memorial in Xiu's name requesting that inner attendants who had profited by deceit be sifted and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men feared his return to power. Someone forged a memorial in his name calling for the purging of palace eunuchs who had profited through fraud.

sentences.zh: 其群皆怨怒，譖之，出知同州，帝納吳充言而止。

translations.literal: The whole group were resentful and angry and slandered him; he was sent out to be prefect of Tongzhou, but the Emperor accepted Wu Chong's words and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The whole corps grew resentful and slandered him. He was ordered out to serve as Prefect of Tongzhou, but the emperor heeded Wu Chong and stayed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士，俾修《唐書》。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Academician and ordered to compile the History of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician and ordered to compile the History of Tang.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，其主命貴臣四人押宴，曰：「此非常制，以卿名重故爾。」

translations.literal: Sent on mission to the Khitan, their ruler ordered four honored ministers to escort the banquet, saying: "This is not the usual rule—it is because of your great renown."
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Khitan, their ruler ordered four honored ministers to attend his banquet, saying, "This is not the usual custom. It is because of your great renown."

sentences.zh: 知嘉祐二年貢舉。

translations.literal: He supervised the metropolitan examination of the second year of Jiayou.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Jiayou era.

sentences.zh: 時士子尚爲險怪奇澀之文，號「太學體」，修痛排抑之，凡如是者輒黜。

translations.literal: At that time scholars still favored perilous, strange, and harshly obscure writing, called the "Taixue style"; Xiu painfully suppressed it, and all such were forthwith failed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time candidates still favored perilous, strange, and harshly obscure compositions known as the "Taixue style." Xiu rigorously suppressed it, failing every paper of that kind.

sentences.zh: 畢事，向之囂薄者伺修出，聚譟於馬首，街邏不能制；

translations.literal: When the examinations ended, those who had earlier been insolent toward him waited for Xiu to come out and gathered to clamor at his horse's head; the street patrol could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: When the examinations ended, those who had mocked him waited for him to emerge and mobbed his horse, clamoring so loudly that the street patrol could not control them.

sentences.zh: 然場屋之習，從是遂變。

translations.literal: Yet the habits of the examination halls from this time forth were changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from that time the habits of the examination halls were transformed.

sentences.zh: 加龍圖閣學士、知開封府，承包拯威嚴之後，簡易循理，不求赫赫名，京師亦治。

translations.literal: He was added Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and made prefect of Kaifeng. Following Bao Zheng's stern rule, he was easygoing and followed reason, not seeking a resounding name, and the capital was also well governed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and Prefect of Kaifeng. Following Bao Zheng's stern administration, he governed with ease and reason, seeking no resounding reputation, yet the capital was well ordered.

sentences.zh: 旬月，改群牧使。

translations.literal: In a ten-day month he was changed to Commissioner of the Herds.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was transferred to Commissioner of the Herds.

sentences.zh: 《唐書》成，拜禮部侍郎兼翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When the History of Tang was completed, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and concurrent Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the History of Tang was completed, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites and concurrent Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 修在翰林八年，知無不言。

translations.literal: Xiu was in the Hanlin for eight years and in office knew nothing he did not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu spent eight years in the Hanlin Academy and spoke without reserve on every matter within his purview.

sentences.zh: 河決商胡，北京留守賈昌朝欲開橫壟故道，回河使東流。

translations.literal: The Yellow River burst its banks at Shanghu; the administrative coordinator of the Northern Capital, Jia Changchao, wished to open the old course of the Heng dam to turn the river east.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River burst its banks at Shanghu. Jia Changchao, administrative coordinator of the Northern Capital, proposed reopening the old course of the Heng dam to turn the river eastward.

sentences.zh: 有李仲昌者，欲導入六塔河，議者莫知所從。

translations.literal: There was one Li Zhongchang who wished to divert it into the Liuta River; those who discussed it did not know which to follow.
translations.idiomatic: A certain Li Zhongchang proposed diverting it into the Liuta River. The debaters could not decide which plan to adopt.

sentences.zh: 修以爲：「河水重濁，理無不淤，下流既淤，上流必決。

translations.literal: Xiu held: "River water is heavy and turbid; in principle it must silt up. When the lower reaches are silted, the upper reaches must break out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu argued, "Yellow River water is heavy and turbid; by nature it must silt up. When the lower course silts, the upper course must break out.

sentences.zh: 以近事驗之，決河非不能力塞，故道非不能力復，但勢不能久耳。

translations.literal: Verified by recent events, it is not that the river cannot be forcibly blocked when it breaks, nor that the old course cannot be forcibly restored—but the situation cannot long endure.
translations.idiomatic: Recent experience shows that a breach cannot be permanently dammed by force, nor an old course permanently restored—but neither expedient can last.

sentences.zh: 橫壟功大難成，雖成將復決。

translations.literal: The Heng dam project is great and hard to complete; even if completed it will break again.
translations.idiomatic: The Heng dam project is vast and hard to finish; even if finished it will breach again.

sentences.zh: 六塔狹小，而以全河注之，濱、棣、德、博必被其害。

translations.literal: The Liuta is narrow and small, yet the whole river is to be poured into it—Bin, Di, De, and Bo will certainly suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Liuta is narrow and small, yet the whole river would be poured into it. Bin, Di, De, and Bo would certainly suffer disaster.

sentences.zh: 不若因水所趨，增堤峻防，疏其下流，縱使入海，此數十年之利也。」

translations.literal: Better to follow where the water tends, raise the dikes and heighten the defenses, dredge the lower reaches, and let it run into the sea—this is a benefit for several decades."
translations.idiomatic: Better to follow the water's inclination, raise and strengthen the dikes, dredge the lower course, and let the river reach the sea. That would secure several decades of benefit."

sentences.zh: 宰相陳執中主昌朝，文彥博主仲昌，竟爲河北患。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Chen Zhizhong supported Changchao; Wen Yanbo supported Zhongchang; in the end it became a calamity for Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Chen Zhizhong backed Changchao; Wen Yanbo backed Zhongchang. In the end Hebei suffered calamity.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年，參知政事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Participant in Determining Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Participant in Determining Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 修在兵府，與曾明仲考天下兵數及三路屯戍多少、地理遠近，更爲圖籍。

translations.literal: While Xiu was in the military bureau, together with Zeng Gongliang he examined the empire's troop numbers and the garrisons of the three circuits, how many or few, and the distance and nearness of geography, and remade the maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the military bureau, he joined Zeng Gongliang in surveying the empire's troop strength, the garrisons along the three frontier circuits, their numbers, and the distances between posts, and remade the maps and registers.

sentences.zh: 凡邊防久缺屯戍者，必加搜補。

translations.literal: Wherever on the borders long-term garrisons had been lacking, he invariably added search and reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever long-standing gaps in frontier garrisons appeared, he ordered them filled.

sentences.zh: 其在政府，與韓琦同心輔政。

translations.literal: In the government he and Han Qi with one heart assisted in administration.
translations.idiomatic: In government he and Han Qi worked in concert as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 凡兵民、官吏、財利之要，中書所當知者，集爲總目，遇事不復求之有司。

translations.literal: As for all essentials of soldiers, officials, and financial profit that the Secretariat ought to know, he collected them into a general register; when affairs arose one no longer had to seek them from the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: All essentials regarding troops, officials, and revenue that the Secretariat needed to know he compiled into a master register, so that when business arose one no longer had to query the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 時東宮猶未定，與韓琦等協定大議，語在《琦傳》。

translations.literal: At that time the Eastern Palace was still undecided; together with Han Qi and others he settled the great deliberation—the account is in the biography of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the heir apparent had not yet been settled; together with Han Qi and others he resolved the great question of succession—the account appears in Qi's biography.

sentences.zh: 英宗以疾未親政，皇太后垂簾，左右交構，幾成嫌隙。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong, because of illness, had not yet personally governed; the Empress Dowager held the curtain and ruled, and those about her wove intrigues, so that suspicion and estrangement nearly arose.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong, stricken with illness, had not yet taken up personal rule. The Empress Dowager ruled from behind the curtain, and those around her wove intrigues until suspicion and estrangement nearly took hold.

sentences.zh: 韓琦奏事，太后泣語之故。

translations.literal: Han Qi memorialized on affairs; the Empress Dowager wept and told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qi memorialized on state affairs, the Empress Dowager wept and explained the cause of her distress.

sentences.zh: 琦以帝疾爲解，太后意不釋，修進曰：「太后事仁宗數十年，仁德著於天下。

translations.literal: Qi took the emperor's illness as explanation; the Empress Dowager's mind was not released. Xiu advanced and said: "The Empress Dowager served Emperor Renzong for several decades, and her benevolence is manifest throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Qi explained matters in light of the emperor's illness, but the Empress Dowager's heart was not eased. Xiu stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty served Emperor Renzong for decades, and your benevolence is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 昔溫成之寵，太后處之裕如；

translations.literal: In former times, when Wencheng received favor, the Empress Dowager dealt with it at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Wen received the late emperor's favor, you bore it with composure.

sentences.zh: 今母子之間，反不能容邪？」

translations.literal: Now between mother and son, can you not contain it?"
translations.idiomatic: Can you not now make room for the bond between mother and son?"

sentences.zh: 太后意稍和，修復曰：「仁宗在位久，德澤在人。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's mood eased somewhat; Xiu spoke again: "Emperor Renzong was on the throne long, and his virtue and grace abide in the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager softened a little. Xiu went on: "Emperor Renzong reigned for many years, and his kindness still lives in the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 故一日晏駕，天下奉戴嗣君，無一人敢異同者。

translations.literal: Therefore when in a single day he passed away, the whole realm accepted and upheld the successor, and not one person dared to dissent.
translations.idiomatic: So when he died in a single day, the whole realm rallied to the heir, and not a soul dared raise a contrary word.

sentences.zh: 今太后一婦人，臣等五六書生耳，非仁宗遺意，天下誰肯聽從。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is but one woman, and we your ministers are but five or six bookish scholars—if this were not Emperor Renzong's dying wish, who in the realm would heed us?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is one woman; we are five or six scholars with books in our hands. If this were not what Renzong intended at his death, who under heaven would listen to us?"

sentences.zh: 太后默然，久之而罷。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was silent; after a long while she dismissed the audience.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said nothing. After a long silence she dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 修平生與人盡言無所隱。

translations.literal: Throughout his life Xiu spoke his whole mind to others and concealed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: All his life Xiu spoke plainly to others and hid nothing.

sentences.zh: 及執政，士大夫有所干請，輒面諭可否，雖臺諫官論事，亦必以是非詰之，以是怨誹益眾。

translations.literal: When he came to power, whenever scholar-officials made requests he would face them and declare what was permitted or forbidden; even when remonstrance officials discussed affairs he would press them with right and wrong—thus resentments and slanders grew all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, whenever gentlemen sought his favor he told them to their faces what he would or would not do. Even remonstrance officials who came to debate policy he cross-examined on right and wrong. For this, resentment and slander against him only multiplied.

sentences.zh: 帝將追崇濮王，命有司議，皆謂當稱皇伯，改封大國。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to posthumously honor the Prince of Pu; he ordered the relevant offices to deliberate, and all said he ought to be styled Imperial Uncle and his fief enlarged to a great state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to honor his biological father, the Prince of Pu, after death. He ordered the ministries to deliberate. All agreed he should be called Imperial Uncle and enfeoffed as ruler of a great state.

sentences.zh: 修引《喪服記》，以爲：「『爲人後者，爲其父母服』，降三年為期，而不沒父母之名，以見服可降而名不可沒也。

translations.literal: Xiu cited the 《Records of Mourning Garments》, arguing: "'One who becomes another's heir still wears mourning for his natural parents'—the three-year mourning is reduced to one year, yet the parents' names are not erased, showing that mourning may be reduced but names may not be effaced.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu cited the 《Records of Mourning Garments》, saying: "'One who becomes another's heir still mourns his natural parents'—three years of mourning are reduced to one, yet the parents' names are not erased. This shows that the period of mourning may be shortened, but the bond of kinship may not be wiped away.

sentences.zh: 若本生之親，改稱皇伯，歷考前世，皆無典據。

translations.literal: If one's biological parents were retitled Imperial Uncle, a survey of all previous ages finds no canonical precedent.
translations.idiomatic: To retitle one's biological parents as Imperial Uncle—search every prior age and you will find no precedent in the canon of ritual.

sentences.zh: 進封大國，則又禮無加爵之道。

translations.literal: To advance enfeoffment to a great state likewise has no path in ritual for adding rank.
translations.idiomatic: To advance the enfeoffment to a great state is likewise to add rank where ritual provides no means of doing so.

sentences.zh: 故中書之議，不與眾同。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Secretariat's proposal did not agree with the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the Secretariat's view did not match the consensus."

sentences.zh: 太后出手書，許帝稱親，尊王爲皇，王夫人爲后。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued a handwritten edict permitting the emperor to address his father as kin, honoring the prince as emperor and his lady as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager issued a letter in her own hand, permitting the emperor to call his father by the name of kin, honoring the prince as emperor and his consort as empress.

sentences.zh: 帝不敢當。

translations.literal: The emperor did not dare accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not dare accept.

sentences.zh: 於是御史呂誨等詆修主此議，爭論不已，皆被逐。

translations.literal: Thereupon the investigating censor Lü Hui and others denounced Xiu as chief advocate of this proposal; they argued without cease and were all driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Then the investigating censor Lü Hui and others attacked Xiu as the chief architect of this policy. They wrangled without end and were all expelled from court.

sentences.zh: 惟蔣之奇之說合修意，修薦爲御史，眾目爲奸邪。

translations.literal: Only Jiang Zhiqi's view accorded with Xiu's intent; Xiu recommended him as investigating censor, but common eyes marked him as wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jiang Zhiqi's position matched Xiu's. Xiu recommended him for investigating censor, but in the eyes of the court he was counted among the corrupt.

sentences.zh: 之奇患之，則思所以自解。

translations.literal: Zhiqi was troubled by this and sought a way to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi was uneasy at this and cast about for a way to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 修婦弟薛宗孺有憾於修，造帷薄不根之謗摧辱之，輾轉達於中丞彭思永，思永以告之奇，之奇即上章劾修。

translations.literal: Xiu's brother-in-law Xue Zongru bore a grudge against Xiu and fabricated baseless scandal of curtain intimacy to destroy him; it passed from hand to hand until it reached Vice Censor-in-Chief Peng Siyong, who told Zhiqi, and Zhiqi at once submitted a memorial impeaching Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's brother-in-law Xue Zongru, who bore him a grudge, invented groundless tales of illicit intimacy behind the curtain to ruin him. The rumor wound its way to the vice censor-in-chief Peng Siyong, who relayed it to Zhiqi, and Zhiqi at once memorialized the throne to impeach Xiu.

sentences.zh: 神宗初即位，欲深護修。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong had just ascended the throne, he wished to shield Xiu deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong first took the throne, he wished to protect Xiu to the full.

sentences.zh: 訪故宮臣孫思恭，思恭爲辨釋，修杜門請推治。

translations.literal: He consulted the former palace attendant Sun Sigong, who offered an explanation on Xiu's behalf; Xiu shut his doors and asked that the matter be thoroughly investigated.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out the former palace attendant Sun Sigong, who spoke in Xiu's defense. Xiu closed his doors and asked that the charges be pursued to the end.

sentences.zh: 帝使詰思永、之奇，問所從來，辭窮，皆坐黜。

translations.literal: The emperor had Siyong and Zhiqi interrogated and asked whence it came; their words exhausted, both were punished with dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Siyong and Zhiqi questioned and asked where the tale originated. Their answers failed them, and both were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 修亦力求退，罷爲觀文殿學士、刑部尚書、知亳州。

translations.literal: Xiu also pressed hard to retire and was removed to Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Minister of Justice, and Prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu pressed equally hard to withdraw. He was relieved as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Minister of Justice, and prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷兵部尚書、知青州，改宣徽南院使、判太原府。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Minister of War and Prefect of Qingzhou, then changed to Commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat and Acting Administrator of Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was moved to Minister of War and prefect of Qingzhou, then appointed commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat with concurrent authority over Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 辭不拜，徙蔡州。

translations.literal: He declined to accept the post and was moved to Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the appointment and was transferred to Cai Prefecture instead.

sentences.zh: 修以風節自持，既數被污蔑，年六十，即連乞謝事，帝輒優詔弗許。

translations.literal: Xiu held himself by integrity and moral bearing; having been slandered many times, at age sixty he repeatedly begged to resign office, yet the emperor each time issued gracious edicts refusing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu held himself by integrity. Slandered again and again, at sixty he repeatedly petitioned to leave office, yet each time the emperor answered with a gracious edict that would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 及守青州，又以請止散青苗錢，爲安石所詆，故求歸愈切。

translations.literal: When he governed Qingzhou he again asked to halt distribution of green sprout loans and was reviled by An Shi, so his wish to return home grew all the keener.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Qingzhou he again asked that distribution of green sprout money be stopped. Wang Anshi denounced him for it, and his longing to go home grew only more urgent.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，以太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining he retired as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Xining reign he retired with the rank of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，贈太子太師，諡曰文忠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; posthumously honored as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died. He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Loyal in Culture.

sentences.zh: 修始在滁州，號「醉翁」，晚更號「六一居士」。

translations.literal: Xiu first in Chuzhou took the sobriquet "Old Drunkard"; in later years he changed it to "Hermit of Six Ones."
translations.idiomatic: While first at Chuzhou, Xiu styled himself the Old Drunkard; in later years he took instead the name Hermit of Six Ones.

sentences.zh: 天資剛勁，見義勇爲，雖機阱在前，觸發之不顧。

translations.literal: His natural endowment was firm and forceful; when he saw righteousness he acted bravely; though snares lay before him he triggered them without regard.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was hard and unyielding. Where he saw the right he acted without fear. Though traps lay before him, he sprang them and did not look back.

sentences.zh: 放逐流離，至於再三，志氣自若也。

translations.literal: Exiled and cast adrift, time and again, his spirit and ambition remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Banished and driven from place to place, again and again, his spirit remained what it had always been.

sentences.zh: 方貶夷陵時，無以自遣，因取舊案反覆觀之，見其枉直乖錯不可勝數，於是仰天歎曰：「以荒遠小邑，且如此，天下固可知。」

translations.literal: While exiled to Yiling, having no way to distract himself, he took old case files and examined them repeatedly, seeing wrong and right tangled beyond counting; he then sighed to heaven: "In a remote petty district it is already thus—the realm may be known indeed."
translations.idiomatic: While banished to Yiling, with nothing to occupy his mind, he took old case files and went through them again and again. Wrong and right were twisted beyond counting. He looked up to heaven and sighed: "If a remote little county is already like this, the realm as a whole may be known."

sentences.zh: 自爾，遇事不敢忽也。

translations.literal: From that time he dared not neglect any matter that came his way.
translations.idiomatic: From that day on, he never dared treat any affair lightly.

sentences.zh: 學者求見，所與言，未嘗及文章，惟談吏事，謂文章止於潤身，政事可以及物。

translations.literal: When scholars sought audience, what he spoke of with them never touched literary composition but only discussed administrative affairs, saying that writing serves only to polish the self whereas governance can reach outward to things.
translations.idiomatic: When students came seeking him, he never spoke of literature, only of the business of office. Writing, he said, polishes only the self; government can reach out and touch the world.

sentences.zh: 凡歷數郡，不見治跡，不求聲譽，寬簡而不擾，故所至民便之。

translations.literal: In every prefecture he passed through there was no visible trace of governance nor pursuit of reputation—lenient and simple without disturbance, so wherever he went the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In every commandery he held, he left no show of administrative feats and sought no renown. He governed with ease and restraint, troubling no one, so wherever he went the people were at their ease.

sentences.zh: 或問：「爲政寬簡，而事不弛廢，何也？」

translations.literal: Someone asked: "Governing with lenience and simplicity, yet affairs are not neglected—how is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him: "You govern with lenience and simplicity, yet nothing is neglected—how is that?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「以縱爲寬，以略爲簡，則政事弛廢，而民受其弊。

translations.literal: He said: "If lenience means indulgence and simplicity means neglect, then administration is neglected and the people suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "If lenience means letting everything go and simplicity means overlooking everything, then government falls into neglect and the people suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 吾所謂寬者，不爲苛急；

translations.literal: What I call lenience is not being harsh and urgent;
translations.idiomatic: What I mean by lenience is not to be harsh and pressing;

sentences.zh: 簡者，不爲繁碎耳。」

translations.literal: what I call simplicity is not being fragmented and minutely burdensome."
translations.idiomatic: what I mean by simplicity is not to burden people with petty, fragmented rules."

sentences.zh: 修幼失父，母嘗謂曰：「汝父爲吏，常夜燭治官書，屢廢而歎。

translations.literal: Xiu lost his father in youth; his mother once said to him: "Your father served as an official and would often burn the midnight lamp over government documents, repeatedly laying them aside and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu lost his father young. His mother once told him: "Your father served as an official. He would work by lamplight deep into the night over the papers of office, then set them down again and again and sigh.

sentences.zh: 吾問之，則曰：『死獄也，我求其生，不得爾。』

translations.literal: I asked him, and he said: 'A death-case in the prison—I seek life for him and cannot obtain it.'
translations.idiomatic: I asked why. He said: 'A man condemned to die in prison—I am trying to find a way for him to live, and I cannot.'

sentences.zh: 吾曰：『生可求乎？』

translations.literal: I said: 'Can life be sought?' He said:'
translations.idiomatic: I said: 'Can a life be sought?' He said:'

sentences.zh: 曰：『求其生而不得，則死者與我皆無恨。

translations.literal: When I seek life and cannot obtain it, then he who dies and I alike have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: When I seek life and cannot find it, then the condemned man and I alike will have no regret.

sentences.zh: 夫常求其生，猶失之死，而世常求其死也。』

translations.literal: For if one constantly seeks life for a man yet still loses him to death, while the world constantly seeks a man's death.'
translations.idiomatic: For if one constantly seeks a man's life yet still loses him to death, while the world constantly seeks a man's death.'

sentences.zh: 其平居教他子弟，常用此語，吾耳熟焉。」

translations.literal: In ordinary times teaching other sons he always used this saying—I heard it until my ears knew it by heart."
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary times, teaching the other boys, he always used this saying. I heard it until it was worn into my ears."

sentences.zh: 修聞而服之終身。

translations.literal: When Xiu heard it he submitted to it all his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu heard this he took it to heart for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 爲文天才自然，豐約中度。

translations.literal: In writing his heaven-given talent was natural, full or spare in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: As a writer his gift was innate, his fullness and restraint always in balance.

sentences.zh: 其言簡而明，信而通，引物連類，折之於至理，以服人心。

translations.literal: His words were brief yet clear, trustworthy yet penetrating; citing things he linked their kinds and broke them down to ultimate principle, thereby winning people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was spare yet luminous, sure yet far-reaching. He drew examples and bound them into classes, pressing each argument to its root principle until hearts were won.

sentences.zh: 超然獨騖，眾莫能及，故天下翕然師尊之。

translations.literal: He soared alone beyond the herd; none could keep pace—thus the realm as one accorded him the honor of master.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged alone above the crowd, and none could follow. For this the realm, as one, took him for its teacher.

sentences.zh: 獎引後進，如恐不及，賞識之下，率為聞人。

translations.literal: He encouraged and drew forward the rising generation as though fearing to fall short; those he recognized and favored mostly became men of renown.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted up the young as though he feared he might not do enough. Of those he marked out for praise, most in time became celebrated names.

sentences.zh: 曾鞏、王安石、蘇洵、洵子軾、轍，布衣屏處，未爲人知，修即遊其聲譽，謂必顯於世。

translations.literal: Zeng Gong, Wang Anshi, Su Xun, Xun's sons Shi and Zhe—in commoner garb, secluded, not yet known to the world—Xiu at once sought out word of them and said they would surely shine in their age.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gong, Wang Anshi, Su Xun, and Xun's sons Shi and Zhe were then in plain dress, living apart, unknown to the world. Xiu sought out reports of them at once and declared that they would surely rise to prominence.

sentences.zh: 篤於朋友，生則振掖之，死則調護其家。

translations.literal: He was devoted to friends: while they lived he would uplift and support them; when they died he would look after their households.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to his friends, he lifted them up while they lived and saw to their families after they died.

sentences.zh: 好古嗜學，凡周、漢以降金石遺文、斷編殘簡，一切掇拾，研稽異同，立說於左，的的可表證，謂之《集古錄》。

translations.literal: He loved antiquity and was addicted to learning. From Zhou and Han onward, every metal-and-stone inscription and every torn fascicle or broken slip—he gathered them all, investigated and compared their discrepancies, set explanations in the margin wherever they could be clearly verified, and called the work 《Collected Records of Antiquities》.
translations.idiomatic: A lover of antiquity and a voracious scholar, he collected every surviving inscription and fragment from Zhou and Han down, collated their discrepancies, annotated what could be firmly established, and published the result as 《Collected Records of Antiquities》.

sentences.zh: 奉詔修《唐書》紀、志、表，自撰《五代史記》，法嚴詞約，多取《春秋》遺旨。

translations.literal: By imperial order he compiled the annals, treatises, and tables of the 《Book of Tang》; on his own he wrote 《Records of the Five Dynasties》—its method stern, its words sparse, drawing heavily on the leftover intents of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered by the throne to edit the annals, treatises, and tables of the 《Book of Tang》, he also authored on his own the 《Records of the Five Dynasties》—austere in method and spare in diction, steeped in the spirit of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾敘其文曰：「論大道似韓愈，論事似陸贄，記事似司馬遷，詩賦似李白。」

translations.literal: Su Shi described his writings, saying: "In discussing the Great Way he is like Han Yu; in discussing affairs he is like Lu Zhi; in recording events he is like Sima Qian; in poetry and rhapsody he is like Li Bo."
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi summed up his prose thus: "On the Great Way he reads like Han Yu; on policy, like Lu Zhi; in narrative history, like Sima Qian; in verse and fu, like Li Bo."

sentences.zh: 識者以爲知言。

translations.literal: Those who understood such things took this for discerning speech.
translations.idiomatic: Connoisseurs judged that a true appraisal.

sentences.zh: 子 發

translations.literal: Son: Fa
translations.idiomatic: Son: Fa

sentences.zh: 子發，字伯和，少好學，師事安定胡瑗，得古樂鍾律之說，不治科舉文詞，獨探古始立論議。

translations.literal: Zi Fa, courtesy name Bohe, loved learning from youth. He took Hu Yuan of Anding as his teacher and mastered the theories of ancient music's bells and pitch pipes. He did not pursue examination essays but alone plumbed antiquity's beginnings to establish discourses.
translations.idiomatic: Fa, whose courtesy name was Bohe, was studious from boyhood. He studied under Hu Yuan of Anding and mastered theories of ancient pitch pipes and bell-tones, shunned the examination essay, and devoted himself instead to probing antiquity and framing original arguments.

sentences.zh: 自書契以來，君臣世系，制度文物，旁及天文、地理，靡不悉究。

translations.literal: From the invention of writing onward—lines of sovereign and minister, institutions and cultural artifacts, extending even to astronomy and geography—there was nothing he did not investigate exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of written records he pursued everything—royal and ministerial lines, institutions and material culture, even astronomy and geography—until nothing lay outside his inquiry.

sentences.zh: 以父恩，補將作監主薄，賜進士出身，累遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: Through his father's favor he was appointed registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings, was granted jinshi status, and was repeatedly promoted to vice director of the Bureau of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to his father's standing he entered service as registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings, received jinshi standing by grace, and rose in stages to vice director of the Bureau of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: He died at forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾哭之，以謂發得文忠公之學，漢伯喈、晉茂先之流也。

translations.literal: Su Shi mourned him, saying that Fa had obtained the learning of Duke of Letters Wengong, and was of the same sort as Bohe of Han and Maoxian of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi lamented his death, declaring that Fa had inherited Wengong's learning and stood in the line of Han's Cai Yong and Jin's Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 子 棐

translations.literal: Son: Fei
translations.idiomatic: Son: Fei

sentences.zh: 中子棐，字叔弼，廣覽強記，能文辭，年十三時，見修著《鳴蟬賦》，侍側不去。

translations.literal: The middle son, Fei, courtesy name Shubi, read widely and remembered strongly, and was skilled at literary composition. When he was thirteen he saw Xiu writing the 《Cicada Chirping Rhapsody》 and stood at his side refusing to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The middle son Fei, courtesy name Shubi, read voraciously, remembered effortlessly, and wrote well. At thirteen he watched Xiu compose the 《Cicada Chirping Rhapsody》 and would not leave his side.

sentences.zh: 修撫之曰：「兒異日能為吾此賦否？」

translations.literal: Xiu stroked his head and said, "My boy, can you someday write this rhapsody for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu stroked his head and asked, "Child, will you one day write this rhapsody for me?"

sentences.zh: 因書以遺之。

translations.literal: He thereupon copied it out and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Then he copied it out and gave it to him as a keepsake.

sentences.zh: 用蔭，為秘書省正字，登進士乙科，調陳州判官，以親老不仕。

translations.literal: Through hereditary privilege he became proofreader in the Palace Library, passed the jinshi examination in the second class, was assigned as judge of Chen prefecture, but because his parents were elderly he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he became a Palace Library proofreader, passed the jinshi examination in the second class, and was posted as judge of Chenzhou, but declined to serve because his parents were old.

sentences.zh: 修卒，代草遺表，神宗讀而愛之，意修自作也。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Fei drafted the final memorial in his stead. Emperor Shenzong read it and was delighted, thinking Xiu himself had written it.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu's death Fei drafted the death memorial in his place. Shenzong read it with admiration and assumed Xiu had written it himself.

sentences.zh: 服除，始為審官主簿，累遷職方員外郎、知襄州。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he first served as registrar in the Court for the Examination of Credentials, and was repeatedly promoted to assistant director in the Bureau of Military Appointments and prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he entered office as registrar in the Court for Examination of Credentials, then rose through assistant director in the Bureau of Military Appointments to prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾布執政，其婦兄魏泰倚聲勢來居襄，規占公私田園，強市民貨，郡縣莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: When Zeng Bu held power, his wife's elder brother Wei Tai relied on that influence to come live at Xiang, scheming to seize public and private fields and gardens and forcibly buying goods from townspeople—yet no county or district dared resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zeng Bu's administration, Bu's brother-in-law Wei Tai traded on that power to settle in Xiangzhou, grabbing public and private land and extorting townspeople's goods while no local office dared stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 至是，指州門東偏官邸廢址為天荒，請之。

translations.literal: At this time he pointed to the ruined site of an official residence east of the prefectural gate and called it "heaven's waste," requesting it.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he designated the abandoned government quarters east of the prefectural gate as "imperial waste" and petitioned for them.

sentences.zh: 吏具成牘至，棐曰：「孰謂州門之東偏而有天荒乎？」

translations.literal: When clerks presented the completed documents, Fei said, "Who says that east of the prefectural gate there is any heaven's waste?"
translations.idiomatic: When the clerks brought the finished paperwork, Fei said, "Who ever heard of 'heaven's waste' east of the prefectural gate?

sentences.zh: 卻之。

translations.literal: He refused it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the request.

sentences.zh: 眾共白曰：「泰橫于漢南久，今求地而緩與之，且不可，而又可卻邪？」

translations.literal: The crowd together reported to him, saying, "Tai has bullied the Han River region long enough. Now he seeks land and even to grant it slowly is impossible—how then can we refuse it?"
translations.idiomatic: His staff pleaded as one: "Tai has tyrannized the Han River south for years. Even a slow grant of land is unthinkable—how can we refuse him outright?"

sentences.zh: 棐竟持不與。

translations.literal: Fei in the end held firm and would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Fei held his ground and never yielded the land.

sentences.zh: 泰怒，譖於布，徙知潞州，旋又罷去。

translations.literal: Tai grew angry and slandered him to Bu. Fei was transferred to be prefect of Luzhou, and shortly afterward was dismissed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Tai, enraged, slandered him to Zeng Bu. Fei was reassigned as prefect of Luzhou, then soon dismissed altogether.

sentences.zh: 元符末，還朝。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanfu era he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Yuanfu reign he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 曆吏部、右司二郎中，以直秘閣知蔡州。

translations.literal: He successively served in the Ministry of Personnel and as second-rank director in the Right Office; with the title of academician on call in the Hanlin he was made prefect of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn in the Ministry of Personnel and as second-rank director in the Right Office, then, as Hanlin academician on call, became prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡地薄賦重，轉運使又為覆折之令，多取於民，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Cai territory was poor but its taxes heavy, and the transport commissioner also issued orders for double assessment, taking yet more from the people until they could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Caizhou was a poor region with crushing levies; the transport commissioner added orders for double assessment, squeezing the people past endurance.

sentences.zh: 會有詔禁止，而佐吏憚使者，不敢以詔旨從事。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict forbade this, but the aides feared the commissioner and dared not carry out the edict.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then forbade the practice, yet the staff feared the commissioner and would not enforce the throne's command.

sentences.zh: 棐曰：「州郡之於民，詔令苟有未便，猶將建請。

translations.literal: Fei said, "As between a prefecture and its people, if an edict should in any way be inconvenient, one must still petition the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Fei said, "Between a prefecture and its people, even when an edict seems awkward, officials should still memorialize the throne.

sentences.zh: 今天子詔意深厚，知覆折之病民，手詔止之。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven's edict is steeped in humane intent: knowing that double assessment harms the people, he personally wrote an edict to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Today's edict is steeped in humane intent: the Son of Heaven knows double assessment harms the people and has personally written to halt it.

sentences.zh: 若有憚而不行，何以爲長吏？」

translations.literal: If we fear and do not execute it, how can we call ourselves chief officials?"
translations.idiomatic: If we shrink back and refuse to act, what sort of chief officials are we?"

sentences.zh: 命即日行之。

translations.literal: He ordered it carried out that same day.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it enforced that very day.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐黨籍廢，十餘年卒。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed on account of the faction list; he died more than ten years later.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was cashiered on the faction register; he died more than a decade afterward.

sentences.zh: 論曰：三代而降，薄乎秦、漢，文章雖與時盛衰，而藹如其言，曄如其光，皦如其音，蓋均有先王之遺烈。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: From the Three Dynasties downward it grew thin—down to Qin and Han. Though literature waxed and waned with the times, it was lush as their words, bright as their light, clear as their sound: all alike bore something of the former kings' surviving glory.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal runs: After the Three Dynasties culture thinned toward Qin and Han. Literature rose and fell with the age, yet remained lush in word, radiant in brilliance, and pure in tone—each age still carrying some trace of the former kings' legacy.

sentences.zh: 涉晉、魏而弊，至唐韓愈氏振起之。

translations.literal: Passing through Jin and Wei it declined; by Tang, Master Han Yu revived it.
translations.idiomatic: Through Jin and Wei it sickened; in Tang, Han Yu raised it up again.

sentences.zh: 唐之文，涉五季而弊，至宋歐陽修又振起之。

translations.literal: Tang literature, passing through the Five Dynasties, declined again; in Song, Ouyang Xiu once more revived it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang letters, worn down across the Five Dynasties, found renewal in Song through Ouyang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 挽百川之頹波，息千古之邪說，使斯文之正氣，可以羽翼大道，扶持人心，此兩人之力也。

translations.literal: They turned back the myriad streams' collapsing waves and stilled a thousand years' wicked doctrines, so that the orthodox breath of this culture could wing the Great Way and uphold the human heart—these two men's power.
translations.idiomatic: They turned back the collapsing tide of ten thousand streams and quelled a millennium of heterodox talk, so that the orthodox breath of civilization could again wing the Great Way and shore up the human heart—such was the force of these two men.

sentences.zh: 愈不獲用，修用矣，亦弗克究其所爲，可爲世道惜也哉！

translations.literal: Yu was not employed; Xiu was employed—yet he too could not fully carry out what he meant to do. One may lament this for the age!
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu never won full employment; Xiu did, yet could not finish what he set out to do. The age itself is worth grieving.

sentences.zh: 劉敞，字原父，臨江新喻人。

translations.literal: Liu Chang, courtesy name Yuanfu, was a native of Xinyu in Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, courtesy name Yuanfu, came from Xinyu in Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 舉慶曆進士，廷試第一。

translations.literal: He passed the Qingli jinshi examination and took first place in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Qingli jinshi examination and ranked first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 編排官王堯臣，其內兄也，以親嫌自列，乃以爲第二。

translations.literal: The arranging official Wang Yaochen was his wife's elder brother; citing kinship he withdrew his own name, and accordingly he was placed second.
translations.idiomatic: The arranging official Wang Yaochen was his wife's elder brother; citing conflict of interest he withdrew himself, and was ranked second instead.

sentences.zh: 通判蔡州，直集賢院，判尚書考功。

translations.literal: He was made transit judge of Cai prefecture, academician on call in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and reviewer in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as transit intendant of Caizhou, academician on call in the Hall for Assembling the Worthies, and reviewer in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 夏竦薨，賜諡文正。

translations.literal: When Xia Song died, the posthumous title Wenzheng was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Song died, the posthumous name Wenzheng was granted.

sentences.zh: 敞言：「諡者，有司之事，竦行不應法。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Posthumous titles are the business of the proper offices; Song's conduct does not meet the standards of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Chang argued, "Posthumous names belong to the proper offices; Song's conduct does not satisfy the statutes.

sentences.zh: 今百司各得守其職，而陛下侵臣官。」

translations.literal: Now every bureau may guard its own duties—yet Your Majesty is encroaching on your ministers' offices."
translations.idiomatic: Every department should keep to its charge—yet Your Majesty is trespassing on your ministers' functions."

sentences.zh: 疏三上，改諡文莊。

translations.literal: After three successive memorials it was changed to Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: After three successive memorials the title was revised to Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 方議定大樂，使中貴人參其間，敞諫曰：「王事莫重於樂。

translations.literal: Just then there was debate on fixing the great music, and the court sent palace eunuchs to participate. Chang remonstrated, saying, "Of all royal affairs none outweighs music.
translations.idiomatic: As the court debated the great music, palace eunuchs were sent to take part. Chang remonstrated: "Among royal affairs none outweighs music.

sentences.zh: 今儒學滿朝，辨論有餘，而使若趙談者參之，臣懼爲袁盎笑也。」

translations.literal: Today the court is full of Confucian learning and there is more than enough debate—yet to let men like Zhao Tan participate, I fear we will become a laughingstock to Yuan Ang."
translations.idiomatic: The court today overflows with Confucian scholars and debate—yet if men like Zhao Tan are allowed in, I fear Yuan Ang's laughter will be on us again."

sentences.zh: 權度支判官，徙三司使。

translations.literal: He served as acting fiscal controller, then was moved to commissioner of the three fiscal departments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting fiscal controller, then was transferred to commissioner of the three fiscal departments.

sentences.zh: 秦州與羌人爭古渭地，仁宗問敞：「棄守孰便？」

translations.literal: Qinzhou and the Qiang contested the ancient Guwei lands; Emperor Renzong asked Chang: "Which is better—to abandon or to defend?"
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou and the Qiang were fighting over the old Guwei territory when Emperor Renzong asked Chang, "Would it be better to give it up or hold it?"

sentences.zh: 敞曰：「若新城可以蔽秦州，長無羌人之虞，傾國守焉可也；

translations.literal: Chang said: "If New City can screen Qinzhou and keep it free of Qiang trouble for long, then devoting the whole state to defending it would be acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied, "If New City can shield Qinzhou and keep the Qiang at bay for good, then pouring the nation's strength into holding it would be justified;

sentences.zh: 或地形險利，賊乘之以擾我邊鄙，傾國爭焉可也。

translations.literal: or if the terrain is strategically advantageous and the enemy could use it to harass our borderlands, then devoting the whole state to contesting it would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: or if the ground is strategically vital and the enemy could use it to harry our frontier, then pouring the nation's strength into fighting for it would likewise be justified.

sentences.zh: 今何所重輕，而殫財困民，捐士卒之命以規小利，使曲在中國，非計也。」

translations.literal: But now, what is worth the weight given? Yet we exhaust wealth and burden the people, throw away soldiers' lives to seek a small gain, and let the wrong rest with China—this is no sound plan."
translations.idiomatic: As things stand, what is there to weigh? Yet we drain the treasury, burden the people, and spend soldiers' lives for a trifling gain, putting our own side in the wrong—this is no sound policy."

sentences.zh: 議者多不同，秦州自是多事矣。

translations.literal: Most counselors disagreed, and Qinzhou from then on had many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the counselors disagreed, and from that time Qinzhou knew nothing but trouble.

sentences.zh: 溫成后追冊，有佞人獻議，求立忌。

translations.literal: When Empress Wencheng was posthumously ennobled, a sycophant offered a proposal seeking to establish taboos.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wencheng received a posthumous ennoblement, a flatterer submitted a plan to institute name taboos on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 敞曰：「豈可以私昵之故，變古越禮乎？」

translations.literal: Chang said: "How can one, for the sake of private affection, alter ancient ways and overstep ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "How can private fondness be allowed to overturn ancient precedent and breach ritual?"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: And it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was halted.

sentences.zh: 吳充以典禮得罪，馮京救之，亦罷近職，敞因對極論之，帝曰：「充能官，京亦亡它，中書惡其太直，不相容耳。」

translations.literal: Wu Chong offended over ritual matters; Feng Jing rescued him and was also removed from nearby posts. Chang took the occasion of an audience to argue forcefully. The emperor said: "Chong is capable in office; Jing too has no other fault—the Secretariat simply hates that they are too forthright and cannot tolerate them."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong ran afoul of the court over ritual matters; Feng Jing spoke up for him and was likewise stripped of his close posts. Chang used an audience to argue the matter at length. The emperor said, "Chong is fit for office, and Jing has no other fault—the Secretariat simply cannot abide men so blunt."

sentences.zh: 敞曰：「陛下寬仁好諫，而中書乃排逐言者，是蔽君之明，止君之善也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Your Majesty is generous and welcomes remonstrance, yet the Secretariat is driving away those who speak—this shades the ruler's clarity and stops the ruler's goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Your Majesty is magnanimous and welcomes remonstrance, yet the Secretariat is hounding away those who speak—this veils Your Majesty's clarity and blocks Your Majesty's goodness.

sentences.zh: 臣恐感動陰陽，有日食、地震、風霾之異。」

translations.literal: I fear we will disturb yin and yang and bring strange portents—eclipse, earthquake, and blinding winds."
translations.idiomatic: I fear heaven and earth will be stirred to answer, and we shall see eclipses, earthquakes, and blinding storms."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, exactly that came to pass.

sentences.zh: 因勸帝收攬威權，無使聰明蔽塞，以消災咎，帝深納之，以同修起居注。

translations.literal: He therefore urged the emperor to gather authority back to himself and not let his brilliance be blocked, to dispel calamities; the emperor deeply accepted this and appointed him co-compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He then urged the emperor to gather power back into his own hands and keep his judgment from being walled off, so that disaster might be dispelled. The emperor took this deeply to heart and made him co-compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 未一月，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: Within less than a month he was promoted to drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In less than a month he was promoted to Drafting Edicts.

sentences.zh: 宰相陳執中惡其斥己，沮止之，帝不聽。

translations.literal: The chief minister Chen Zhizhong hated that he had censured him and tried to obstruct it; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Chen Zhizhong, resenting that Chang had criticized him, tried to block the appointment, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 宦者石全彬領觀察使，意不愜，有慍言，居三日為真，敞封還除書，不草制。

translations.literal: The eunuch Shi Quanbin was given an observation commissioner post and was displeased; he spoke angrily. Within three days it became permanent. Chang sealed and returned the appointment document, refusing to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Shi Quanbin was named an observation commissioner and was not satisfied; he spoke in anger. Within three days the appointment was made permanent. Chang sealed up the commission and sent it back, refusing to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，素習知山川道徑，契丹導之行，自古北口至柳河，回屈殆千里，欲誇示險遠。

translations.literal: On a mission to the Khitan, he was long versed in mountains and roads. The Khitan guided his route from Old Northern Pass to Willow River, winding nearly a thousand li, intending to show off hardship and distance.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, he was already well versed in mountains and routes. The Khitan led him from the Old Northern Pass to Willow River by a detour of nearly a thousand li, intending to impress him with hardship and distance.

sentences.zh: 敞質譯人曰：「自松亭趨柳河，甚徑且易，不數日可抵中京，何爲故道此？」

translations.literal: Chang questioned the interpreter: "From Songting hastening to Willow River is very direct and easy; in a few days one could reach Middle Capital—why take this roundabout way on purpose?"
