translations.idiomatic: Chang pressed the interpreter: "From Songting to Willow River the road is short and easy; Middle Capital could be reached in a few days—why deliberately take this roundabout route?"

sentences.zh: 譯相顧駭愧曰：「實然。

translations.literal: The interpreters looked at each other, startled and ashamed, and said: "Indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: The interpreters glanced at one another, startled and ashamed, and said, "That is true.

sentences.zh: 但通好以來，置驛如是，不敢變也。」

translations.literal: But since friendly relations began, post-houses have been set up this way—we dare not change it."
translations.idiomatic: But ever since relations were opened, relay stations have been laid out on this route, and we dare not alter it."

sentences.zh: 順州山中有異獸，如馬而食虎豹，契丹不能識，問敞，敞曰：「此所謂駮也。」

translations.literal: In the mountains of Shunzhou there was a strange beast, like a horse but eating tigers and leopards. The Khitan did not know it and asked Chang. Chang said: "This is what is called the bo."
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains of Shunzhou there was a strange beast, horse-like yet feeding on tigers and leopards. The Khitan did not recognize it and asked Chang. Chang said, "This is what is called the bo."

sentences.zh: 爲說其音聲形狀，且誦《山海經》、《管子》書曉之，契丹益歎服。

translations.literal: He described its cry, shape, and form, and quoted the 《Classic of Mountains and Seas》 and the 《Guanzi》 to explain it; the Khitan admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: He described its cry, shape, and form, and quoted the 《Classic of Mountains and Seas》 and the 《Guanzi》 to explain it; the Khitan admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 使還，求知揚州。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he requested appointment as prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the mission he sought appointment as prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 狄青起行伍爲樞密使，每出入，小民輒聚觀，至相與推誦其拳勇，至壅馬足不得行。

translations.literal: Di Qing rose from the ranks to become commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Whenever he went in or out, commoners would gather to watch, even pushing and chanting his boxing prowess, until they blocked the horses and he could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing had risen from the ranks to become Military Affairs Commissioner. Whenever he went out or in, common folk would crowd around to watch, even shoving one another and shouting his feats of boxing, until the horses' path was choked and he could not move.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，人心動搖，青益不自安。

translations.literal: The emperor was unwell and hearts wavered; Qing grew all the more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell ill, hearts wavered, and Qing grew ever more ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 敞辭赴郡，爲帝言曰：「陛下幸愛青，不如出之，以全其終。」

translations.literal: As Chang took leave for his prefecture he told the emperor: "Your Majesty favors Qing—would it not be better to send him out and preserve his end peacefully?"
translations.idiomatic: As Chang took leave for his prefecture he told the emperor, "Your Majesty favors Qing—would it not be better to post him elsewhere and let him end his days in peace?"

sentences.zh: 帝頷之，使出諭中書，青乃去位。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded, sent him out to instruct the Secretariat, and Qing then left his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded, sent him out to instruct the Secretariat, and Qing then resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 揚之雷塘，漢雷陂也，舊爲民田。

translations.literal: Yangzhou's Leitang was the Han dynasty's Leipo—it had formerly been common people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou's Leitang was the Han dynasty's Leipo; it had once been farmland held by common people.

sentences.zh: 其後官取瀦水而不償以它田，主皆失業。

translations.literal: Later officials impounded the water without compensating with other fields, and the owners all lost their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Later officials dammed the water without granting other land in compensation, and the owners all lost their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 然塘亦破決不可漕，州復用爲田。

translations.literal: Yet the pond also burst and could not be used for canal transport; the prefecture returned it to fields again.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the pond also broke through and could not serve for transport; the prefecture turned it back to farmland.

sentences.zh: 敞據唐舊券，悉用還民，發運使爭之，敞卒以予民。

translations.literal: Chang relied on Tang-era title deeds and restored it all to the people. The transport commissioner contested it, but Chang in the end gave it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Chang relied on old Tang title deeds and restored the land entirely to the people. The transport commissioner disputed him, but Chang in the end prevailed and returned it to them.

sentences.zh: 天長縣鞫王甲殺人，既具獄，敞見而察其冤，甲畏吏，不敢自直。

translations.literal: In Tianchang county they tried Wang Jia for murder; when the case was complete, Chang saw him and perceived his injustice. Jia feared the clerks and did not dare speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianchang county Wang Jia was tried for murder; when the case was ready for judgment, Chang saw him and sensed his wrongful conviction. Jia feared the clerks and did not dare speak up for himself.

sentences.zh: 敞以委戶曹杜誘，誘不能有所平反，而傅致益牢。

translations.literal: Chang entrusted it to the household census officer Du You, but You could not reverse the verdict and instead made the framing tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Chang handed the matter to the household census officer Du You, but You could not overturn the verdict and instead tightened the fabricated charges.

sentences.zh: 將論囚，敞曰：「冤也。」

translations.literal: As they were about to pass sentence on the prisoner, Chang said: "This is wrongful."
translations.idiomatic: As they were about to sentence the prisoner, Chang said, "This man has been wronged."

sentences.zh: 親按問之。

translations.literal: He personally examined and questioned the case.
translations.idiomatic: He personally reviewed and questioned the case.

sentences.zh: 甲知能爲己直，乃敢告，蓋殺人者，富人陳氏也。

translations.literal: Jia knew someone could speak for him and dared to tell—the killer was actually the wealthy Chen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia knew he now had someone who could clear him and dared to speak—the real killer was a wealthy man of the Chen clan.

sentences.zh: 相傳以爲神明。

translations.literal: People spread the word that he was divine in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: People spread word that his judgment was almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 徙鄆州，鄆比易守，政不治，市邑攘敓公行。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yanzhou; Yan was comparatively easy to govern, yet administration was neglected and market towns saw brawling bandits in the open.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Yanzhou. Yan was comparatively easy to govern, yet the administration had grown slack and market towns were overrun by brawling ruffians who acted with impunity.

sentences.zh: 敞決獄訟，明賞罰，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Chang decided lawsuits, made rewards and punishments clear, and within the circuit all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Chang settled lawsuits, made rewards and punishments unmistakable, and throughout the prefecture order was restored.

sentences.zh: 客行壽張道中，遺一囊錢，人莫敢取，以告里長，里長爲守視，客還，取得之。

translations.literal: A traveler on the road through Shouzhang dropped a bag of money; no one dared take it. They told the village head, who kept watch for the owner; the traveler returned and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: A traveler on the road through Shouzhang dropped a bag of money; no one dared touch it. He told the village head, who stood guard over it until the traveler came back and reclaimed it.

sentences.zh: 又有暮遺物市中者，旦往訪之，故在。

translations.literal: Someone also lost something in the market at dusk; going the next morning to look, it was still there.
translations.idiomatic: Another man lost something in the market at dusk; when he went the next morning to search for it, it was still where he had left it.

sentences.zh: 先是，久旱，地多蝗。

translations.literal: Earlier there had been long drought and locusts in many places.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the region had suffered long drought, and locusts were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 敞至而雨，蝗出境。

translations.literal: When Chang arrived it rained, and the locusts left the territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang arrived, rain fell and the locusts departed the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召糾察在京刑獄。

translations.literal: He was summoned to investigate capital criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as inspector of capital criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 營卒桑達等醉鬥，指斥乘輿。

translations.literal: Camp soldiers Sang Da and others fought while drunk and cursed the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Camp soldiers Sang Da and others, drunk, brawled and reviled the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 皇城使捕送開封，棄達市。

translations.literal: The Imperial City commissioner arrested and sent them to Kaifeng; Da was executed by abandonment in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial City commissioner arrested them and sent them to Kaifeng; Da was executed by abandonment in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 敞移府，問何以不經審訊。

translations.literal: Chang transferred the case to the court and asked why there had been no interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Chang referred the matter to the prefectural court and asked why the men had not been interrogated.

sentences.zh: 府報曰：「近例，凡聖旨及中書、樞密所鞫獄，皆不慮問。」

translations.literal: The office replied: "Recent precedent: whenever cases are tried under imperial rescript or by the Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs, questioning is not applied."
translations.idiomatic: The court reported, "By recent precedent, whenever cases are tried under an imperial rescript or by the Secretariat or the Bureau of Military Affairs, formal interrogation is not conducted."

sentences.zh: 敞奏請一準近格，樞密院不肯行，敞力爭之，詔以其章下府，著爲令。

translations.literal: Chang memorialized requesting that one standard recent regulation apply; the Bureau of Military Affairs refused. Chang argued forcefully; an edict sent his memorial down to the court and made it regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Chang memorialized asking that a single recent standard be followed. The Bureau of Military Affairs refused to comply; Chang argued forcefully until an edict sent his memorial down to the court and established it as law.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐祫享，群臣上尊號，宰相請撰表，敞說止不得，乃上疏曰：「陛下不受徽號且二十年。

translations.literal: At the Jiayou grand ancestral offering, the ministers offered a honorific title; the chief minister asked to compose the tribute document. Chang argued to stop it but could not; he then submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has refused an honorific title for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiayou grand offering, the ministers proposed an honorific title and the chief minister asked to draft the congratulatory memorial. Chang argued against it in vain and then submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty has declined an honorific title for nearly twenty years already.

sentences.zh: 今復加數字，不足盡聖德，而前美並棄，誠可惜也。

translations.literal: Now to add characters again would still not exhaust sage virtue, yet former praises would all be cast aside—truly a pity.
translations.idiomatic: To pile on more characters would still not exhaust Your Majesty's sage virtue, yet every honor already granted would be thrown away—a genuine waste.

sentences.zh: 今歲以來，頗有災異，正當寅畏天命，深自抑損，豈可於此時乃以虛名爲累。」

translations.literal: Since this year there have been rather many disasters and omens; one should reverently fear Heaven's mandate and deeply restrain oneself—how could one at such a time still be burdened by empty names?"
translations.idiomatic: Since the year began, omens and disasters have multiplied. This is the moment to stand in awe of Heaven and strip yourself back—not to let empty titles weigh you down."

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，顧侍臣曰：「我意本謂當爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial, turned to his attendants, and said, "My mind had always held that it should be so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, turned to his attendants, and said, "I always meant it to end this way."

sentences.zh: 遂不受。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: And he declined the honorific.

sentences.zh: 蜀人龍昌期著書傳經，以詭僻惑眾。

translations.literal: A man of Shu, Long Changqi, wrote books and transmitted the classics, using eccentric doctrines to mislead the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Long Changqi of Shu wrote books and lectured on the classics, beguiling the crowd with outlandish doctrines.

sentences.zh: 文彥博薦諸朝，賜五品服。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo recommended him to the court, and fifth-rank court dress was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo brought him to the court's attention, and the emperor bestowed fifth-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 敞與歐陽修俱曰：「昌期違古畔道，學非而博，王制之所必誅，未使即少正卯之刑，已幸矣，又何賞焉。

translations.literal: Chang and Ouyang Xiu together said, "Changqi violates antiquity and rebels against the Way; his learning is unsound yet pretends to breadth—what royal law surely punishes. That he was not immediately given Shao Zhengmao's sentence was already fortunate—why reward him?
translations.idiomatic: Chang and Ouyang Xiu spoke as one: "Changqi turns his back on antiquity and the Way. His learning is hollow, his show of erudition false—exactly what royal institutions exist to punish. That he was not dealt Shao Zhengmao's fate was mercy enough. Why reward him?

sentences.zh: 乞追還詔書，毋使有識之士，窺朝廷深淺。」

translations.literal: We beg that the edict be recalled, lest men of discernment gauge the court's depth."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that the edict be recalled, lest men of judgment take the measure of this court."

sentences.zh: 昌期聞之，懼不敢受賜。

translations.literal: When Changqi heard, he feared and dared not accept the grant.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi heard and, afraid, refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 敞以識論與眾忤，求知永興軍，拜翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Because Chang's outspoken views clashed with others, he sought appointment as military commissioner of Yongxing and was made Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's sharp opinions had set him against the crowd; he asked for Yongxing command and was made Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 大姓范偉爲奸利，冒同姓戶籍五十年，持府縣短長，數犯法。

translations.literal: A powerful clan head, Fan Wei, practiced wicked profit; for fifty years he passed himself off on a household register of the same surname, held leverage over prefectural and county officers, and repeatedly broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wei, head of a great clan, had grown rich on fraud. For fifty years he had ridden a forged register of the same surname, playing prefectural and county officials against one another, breaking the law again and again.

sentences.zh: 敞窮治其事，偉伏罪，長安中讙喜。

translations.literal: Chang prosecuted the matter thoroughly; Wei confessed guilt, and Chang'an rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Chang prosecuted the case to the end. Wei confessed, and Chang'an erupted in celebration.

sentences.zh: 未及受刑，敞召還，判三班院，偉即變前獄，至於四五，卒之付御史決。

translations.literal: Before punishment could be carried out, Chang was recalled and assigned to the Three-Rank Bureau; Wei at once overturned the earlier verdict, as many as four or five times, until at last it was handed to the censorate for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Before sentence could fall, Chang was recalled to the Three-Rank Bureau. Wei promptly reversed the verdict—four or five times—until the censorate took the case and settled it.

sentences.zh: 敞侍英宗講讀，每指事據經，因以諷諫。

translations.literal: Chang attended Emperor Yingzong's lectures, always citing affairs with scriptural warrant, and thereby offered oblique remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Chang attended Yingzong's lectures, citing the classics at every turn and threading remonstrance through the text.

sentences.zh: 時兩宮方有小人間言，諫者或訐而過直。

translations.literal: At the time the two palaces were still troubled by petty men's whispered slanders; remonstrators sometimes impeached with excessive bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: The two palaces were still poisoned by petty men's whispers, and some remonstrators impeached with a bluntness that overshot the mark.

sentences.zh: 敞進讀《太史公書》，至堯授舜以天下，拱而言曰：「舜至側微也，堯禪之以位，天地享之，百姓戴之，非有他道，惟孝友之德，光於上下耳。」

translations.literal: Chang advanced to read from the 《Records of the Grand Historian》; when he reached Yao's yielding the realm to Shun, he bowed with hands folded and said, "Shun rose from the humblest margins; Yao abdicated the throne to him. Heaven and earth rejoiced in it, and the common people revered him—not by any other art, only by the virtue of filial piety and fraternal harmony, shining above and below."
translations.idiomatic: Chang read aloud from the 《Records of the Grand Historian》. At the passage where Yao yields the realm to Shun, he bowed with folded hands and said: "Shun rose from the humblest margin. Yao set the throne in his hands, and Heaven and earth rejoiced, the people looked up to him—not by any other art, only because filial piety and brotherly love lit the world above and below."

sentences.zh: 帝竦體改容，知其以義理諷也。

translations.literal: The emperor straightened his body and changed expression, knowing that he was being admonished through moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stiffened and changed countenance, knowing he had been admonished through principle.

sentences.zh: 皇太后聞之，亦大喜。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager heard, she too was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager heard and was likewise delighted.

sentences.zh: 敞學問淵博，自佛老、卜筮、天文、方藥、山經、地志，皆究知大略。

translations.literal: Chang's learning was vast and deep; from Buddhist and Daoist thought, divination, astronomy, materia medica, mountain classics, and local gazetteers—he had mastered the outlines of all.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's learning ran deep and wide: Buddhism and Daoism, divination, astronomy, materia medica, mountain classics, local gazetteers—he had mastered the outlines of them all.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜視鎮星，謂人曰：「此於法當得土，不然，則生女。」

translations.literal: Once at night he observed Saturn and told others, "By the prognostic rules this should gain Earth; if not, then a daughter will be born."
translations.idiomatic: One night he watched Saturn and told those present, "By the prognostic rules this augurs the earth element; if not, daughters will be born."

sentences.zh: 後數月，兩公主生。

translations.literal: Several months later, two princesses were born.
translations.idiomatic: Months later, two princesses were born.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「歲星往來虛、危間，色甚明盛，當有興于齊者。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Jupiter moves back and forth between Xu and Wei, its color very bright and strong—someone will rise from Qi."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Jupiter shuttles between Xu and Wei, bright and blazing—someone will rise from Qi."

sentences.zh: 歲餘而英宗以齊州防禦使入承大統。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Yingzong entered to succeed the great succession as Defender Commissioner of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year and more later, Yingzong entered to succeed the throne from his post as Defender Commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗得先秦彝鼎數十，銘識奇奧，皆案而讀之，因以考知三代制度，尤珍惜之。

translations.literal: He once obtained several dozen pre-Qin ritual bronzes; their inscriptions were strange and abstruse. He set them out and read them all, and thus came to know the institutions of the Three Dynasties, cherishing them above all.
translations.idiomatic: He once acquired several dozen pre-Qin ritual vessels. Their inscriptions were strange and dense; he laid them out and read every one, and from them reconstructed the institutions of the Three Dynasties. He treasured them above all else.

sentences.zh: 每曰：「我死，子孫以此蒸嘗我。」

translations.literal: He often said, "When I die, let my descendants use these to offer me sacrificial nourishment."
translations.idiomatic: He would say, "When I die, let my descendants use these to feed my spirit in sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 朝廷每有禮樂之事，必就其家以取決焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had matters of ritual and music, it invariably sought his home for a final decision.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court faced ritual or music, it came to his door for the final word.

sentences.zh: 爲文尤贍敏。

translations.literal: In writing he was especially ample and swift.
translations.idiomatic: As a writer he was lavish and swift.

sentences.zh: 掌外制時，將下直，會追封王、主九人，立馬卻坐，頃之，九制成。

translations.literal: While in charge of external edicts, as he was about to go off duty, there came a rush to ennoble nine princes and princesses. He dismounted, turned back and sat; in a moment all nine drafts were complete.
translations.idiomatic: While drafting external edicts he was about to go off duty when word came to ennoble nine princes and princesses at once. He dismounted, turned back to his desk, and in a breath all nine compositions were done.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修每於書有疑，折簡來問，對其使揮筆，答之不停手，修服其博。

translations.literal: Whenever Ouyang Xiu had doubts in a book he sent a note to ask; facing his messenger Chang would wield the brush and answer without pause, and Xiu marveled at his breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Ouyang Xiu hit a doubt in a text he sent a note. Chang would face the messenger, brush in hand, and answer without pause. Xiu marveled at his range.

sentences.zh: 長於《春秋》，爲書四十卷，行於時。

translations.literal: He excelled in the Spring and Autumn Annals and composed a forty-scroll work circulating in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 and wrote a forty-scroll work that circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 弟：攽。

translations.literal: Younger brother: Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Ban.

sentences.zh: 子：奉世。

translations.literal: Son: Fengshi.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Fengshi.

sentences.zh: 弟 攽

translations.literal: Younger Brother Ban
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Ban

sentences.zh: 弟攽，字貢父，與敞同登科，仕州縣二十年，始爲國子監直講。

translations.literal: The younger brother Ban, courtesy name Gongfu, passed the examinations together with Chang, served in prefectures and counties for twenty years, and only then became erudite lecturer in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ban, courtesy name Gongfu, passed the examinations with Chang, spent twenty years in prefectural and county posts, and only then became erudite lecturer in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修、趙槩薦試館職，御史中丞王陶有夙憾，率侍御史蘇寀共排之，攽官已員外郎，才得館閣校勘。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu and Zhao Gai recommended him for a trial palace appointment; Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao bore an old grudge and led Remonstrance Secretary Su Cai to obstruct him together—though Ban's rank was already Vice Director, he gained only a collator post in the palace archive.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu and Zhao Gai recommended him for a palace archive trial. Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Tao, nursing an old grievance, led Remonstrance Secretary Su Cai to block him. Though Ban already held vice-director rank, he won only a collator's post in the palace archive.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，判尚書考功、同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: In the Xining era he served as reviewer of the Ministry of Personnel and associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xining he served as reviewer in the Ministry of Personnel and associate director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 詔封太祖諸孫行尊者爲王，奉太祖後。

translations.literal: An edict ennobled as kings certain grandsons of Taizu of the senior generation, to uphold Taizu's line.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ennobled as kings certain senior grandsons of Taizu, to carry on the Founding Ancestor's line.

sentences.zh: 攽言：「禮，諸侯不得祖天子，當自奉其國之祖。

translations.literal: Ban argued, "By ritual, feudal lords may not take the Son of Heaven as ancestor; each should honor his own state's founder.
translations.idiomatic: Ban argued: "By ritual, feudal lords may not take the Son of Heaven as ancestor. Each should honor his own state's founder.

sentences.zh: 宜崇德昭、德芳之後，世世勿降爵，宗廟祭祀，使之在位，則所以褒揚藝祖者著矣。」

translations.literal: The descendants of Dezhao and Defang should be exalted, their ranks never lowered from generation to generation, and in ancestral temple worship they should occupy their places—then the means of honoring the Founding Ancestor would stand clear."
translations.idiomatic: Exalt the lines of Dezhao and Defang. Let their ranks never fall from generation to generation; let them stand in the ancestral temple in their proper places—then the way to honor the Founding Ancestor will be plain for all to see."

sentences.zh: 後二王紹封，如攽議。

translations.literal: Later the two kings were enfeoffed again, in accordance with Ban's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Later the two kings were enfeoffed anew, as Ban had urged.

sentences.zh: 方更學校貢舉法，攽曰：「本朝選士之制，行之百年，累代將相名卿，皆由此出，而以為未嘗得人，不亦誣哉。

translations.literal: As the school examination system was being revised, Ban said, "Our dynasty's method of selecting scholars has operated for a century; generation after generation of grand ministers and celebrated officials all emerged through it—yet to claim it never produced worthy men, is that not slander?
translations.idiomatic: As the schools and examination system were being overhauled, Ban said: "Our dynasty's way of choosing scholars has run a century. Generation after generation of chancellors and celebrated ministers came through it—and to say it never produced a single worthy man, is that not slander?

sentences.zh: 願因舊貫，毋輕議改法。

translations.literal: I wish to follow the old practice and not lightly discuss changing the law.
translations.idiomatic: Hold to the old practice. Do not lightly reopen the law.

sentences.zh: 夫士修於家，足以成德，亦何待於學官程課督趣之哉。」

translations.literal: When scholars cultivate themselves at home, that suffices to complete virtue—what need is there for school officials' schedules, lessons, and goading?"
translations.idiomatic: A scholar who cultivates himself at home can complete his virtue without school officials' schedules, lessons, and prodding."

sentences.zh: 王安石在經筵，乞講者坐。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi was at the Classics Mat lectern, he begged that the lecturer be seated.
translations.idiomatic: At the Classics Mat, Wang Anshi asked that the lecturer be allowed to sit.

sentences.zh: 攽曰：「侍臣講論於前，不可安坐，避席立語，乃古今常禮。

translations.literal: Ban said, "When attendant ministers discourse before the throne they may not sit at ease; stepping from the mat to speak standing is the constant ritual of antiquity and today.
translations.idiomatic: Ban said: "When a minister lectures before the throne he may not sit at ease. To leave the mat and speak standing is the constant ritual, ancient and present alike.

sentences.zh: 君使之坐，所以示人主尊德樂道也；

translations.literal: When the lord orders one to sit, it is to show the ruler honors virtue and delights in the Way;
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler commands a seat, it is to show that the sovereign honors virtue and delights in the Way;

sentences.zh: 若不命而請，則異矣。」

translations.literal: if without being commanded one requests it, that is irregular."
translations.idiomatic: to request a seat without being commanded is something else entirely."

sentences.zh: 禮官皆同其議，至今仍之。

translations.literal: The ritual officers all agreed with his view; it remains so to this day.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers all agreed. The practice holds to this day.

sentences.zh: 考試開封舉人，與同院王介爭詈，爲監察御史所劾罷。

translations.literal: Examining Kaifeng examination candidates, he quarreled with his colleague Wang Jie of the same bureau and was impeached and dismissed by the investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: While examining Kaifeng candidates he quarreled with his colleague Wang Jie in the same bureau. The investigating censor impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 禮院廷試始用策，初，考官呂惠卿列阿時者在高等，訐直者反居下。

translations.literal: At the Court of Imperial Sacrifices the palace examination first used policy essays; at the outset examiner Lü Huiqing ranked flatterers of the times in the upper grades while those who impeached with bluntness were placed lower.
translations.idiomatic: At the Court of Imperial Sacrifices the palace examination first used policy essays. At the outset the examiner Lü Huiqing placed flatterers of the times in the upper ranks and blunt remonstrators in the lower.

sentences.zh: 攽覆考，悉反之。

translations.literal: Ban reviewed the case and reversed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ban reviewed the case and reversed every verdict.

sentences.zh: 又嘗詒安石書，論新法不便。

translations.literal: He also once sent Wang Anshi a letter arguing that the new laws were inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: He also once wrote Wang Anshi, arguing that the new laws were ill-advised.

sentences.zh: 安石怒摭前過，斥通判泰州，以集賢校理、判登聞檢院、戶部判官知曹州。

translations.literal: Anshi angrily gathered up his past faults, dismissed him as assistant prefect of Taizhou, and appointed him collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, judge of the Court for Memorials to the Throne, and Ministry of Revenue judge with concurrent authority as prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi, enraged, dredged up his past faults, stripped him of his post as assistant prefect of Taizhou, and reassigned him collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, judge of the Court for Memorials to the Throne, and Ministry of Revenue judge with concurrent authority over Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 曹爲盜區，重法不能止。

translations.literal: Cao was a bandit region; severe law could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Caozhou was a haunt of bandits; harsh statutes could not suppress them.

sentences.zh: 攽曰：「民不畏死，奈何以死懼之。」

translations.literal: Ban said: "When the people do not fear death, how can you use death to frighten them?"
translations.idiomatic: Ban said, "When the people do not fear death, how can you frighten them with death?"

sentences.zh: 至，則治尚寬平，盜亦衰息。

translations.literal: When he arrived, his governance was lenient and even-handed, and banditry also declined and ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took office, he governed with lenience and calm, and banditry likewise waned.

sentences.zh: 爲開封府判官，復出爲京東轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as judge of the Kaifeng prefectural court, then went out again as transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of the Kaifeng prefectural court, then was posted again as transport commissioner of the Eastern Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 部吏罷軟不逮者，務全安之。

translations.literal: Subordinate clerks who were weak and incompetent he strove to protect and keep in place.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks who were slack or unequal to their duties he nevertheless strove to shield and keep in post.

sentences.zh: 徙知兗、亳二州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Yan and Bo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to govern Yanzhou and Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 吳居厚代爲轉運使，能奉行法令，致財賦，乃追坐攽廢弛，黜監衡州鹽倉。

translations.literal: Wu Juhou replaced him as transport commissioner; able to carry out laws and orders and bring in revenue, he then traced Ban's negligence back to him and demoted him to overseer of the Hengzhou salt depot.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Juhou succeeded him as transport commissioner. Skilled at enforcing the laws and raising revenue, he then pinned Ban with charges of lax administration and demoted him to overseer of the Hengzhou salt depot.

sentences.zh: 哲宗初，起知襄州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhezong's reign he was recalled to govern Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong first took the throne, Ban was recalled to govern Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為秘書少監，以疾求去，加直龍圖閣、知蔡州。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice director of the Secretariat, begged leave on account of illness, and was given the added title of direct academician in the Hall of Dragon Pictures with authority as prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as vice director of the Secretariat, pleaded illness, and was granted the added title of direct academician in the Hall of Dragon Pictures with concurrent appointment as prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中孫覺、胡宗愈、中書舍人蘇軾、范百祿言：「攽博記能文章，政事侔古循吏，身兼數器，守道不回，宜優賜之告，使留京師。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretary Sun Jue, Hu Zongyu, Secretariat Drafter Su Shi, and Fan Bailu said: "Ban is broadly learned and skilled in literary composition; in administration he matches the ancient model of the compassionate official; he combines many talents and holds to the Way without turning back—he should be graciously granted leave to remain in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Supervising Secretary Sun Jue, Hu Zongyu, Secretariat Drafter Su Shi, and Fan Bailu memorialized: "Ban is broadly learned and masterly in prose; in government he equals the ancient compassionate official; he unites many talents and holds to the Way without wavering. He should be graciously allowed to remain in the capital."

sentences.zh: 至蔡數月，召拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: After several months at Cai he was summoned and appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After a few months at Caizhou he was summoned and appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 請復舊制，建紫微閣於西省。

translations.literal: He requested restoration of the old system and the building of the Purple Micro Pavilion in the western office.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the old system be restored and the Purple Micro Pavilion built in the western office.

sentences.zh: 竟以疾不起，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the end he did not rise on account of illness and died at sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the end illness kept him from office; he died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 攽所著書百卷，尤邃史學。

translations.literal: Ban's authored works numbered a hundred scrolls; he was especially deep in historical studies.
translations.idiomatic: Ban left a hundred scrolls of writing and was especially deep in historical studies.

sentences.zh: 作《東漢刊誤》，爲人所稱。

translations.literal: He wrote 《Corrections to the Eastern Han》, which men praised.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote 《Corrections to the Eastern Han》, which won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 預司馬光修《資治通鑒》，專職漢史。

translations.literal: He took part in Sima Guang's compilation of the 《Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance》, specializing in Han history.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sima Guang in compiling the 《Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance》, with sole charge of the Han annals.

sentences.zh: 爲人疏俊，不修威儀，喜諧謔，數用以招怨悔，終不能改。

translations.literal: As a man he was open and quick-witted, did not cultivate imposing bearing, delighted in wit and banter, and often used these to invite resentment and regret—yet in the end he could not change.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was open and quick-witted, cared little for imposing bearing, and delighted in wit and banter, often drawing resentment on himself—yet he never changed.

sentences.zh: 子 奉世

translations.literal: Son: Fengshi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Fengshi

sentences.zh: 子奉世，字仲馮，天資簡重，有法度。

translations.literal: The son Fengshi, courtesy name Zhongfeng, was by nature simple and grave and possessed measure.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengshi, courtesy name Zhongfeng, was by nature grave and measured.

sentences.zh: 中進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，初置樞密院諸房檢詳文字，以太子中允居吏房。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, when the various bureaus of the Bureau of Military Affairs were first set up to examine and verify documents, he was made junior palace attendant and placed in the personnel bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xining, when the Bureau of Military Affairs first established its bureaus to examine and verify documents, he was made junior palace attendant and assigned to the personnel bureau.

sentences.zh: 先是，進奏院每五日具定本報狀，上樞密院，然後傳之四方。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Memorial Submission Office every five days prepared the fixed-text bulletin and submitted it to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and only then transmitted it to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Memorial Submission Office every five days prepared the fixed-text bulletin for the Bureau of Military Affairs, which then transmitted it to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 而邸吏輒先期報下，或矯爲家書，以入郵置。

translations.literal: But the lodge clerks would report it down in advance, or forge it as family letters to enter the postal relay.
translations.idiomatic: But lodge clerks would leak the bulletin early, or forge it as private letters to slip into the postal relay.

sentences.zh: 奉世乞革定本，去實封，但以通函騰報。

translations.literal: Fengshi requested abolition of the fixed text, removal of the sealed cover, and reporting only by open dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshi asked that the fixed text be abolished, the sealed cover removed, and reporting done only by open dispatch.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 神宗稱其奉職不苟，加集賢校理、檢正中書戶房公事，改刑房，進直史館、國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Shenzong praised his scrupulous service, added the title collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and examiner in the Secretariat's household bureau, moved him to the penal bureau, and advanced him to direct historian and compiler in the National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong praised his scrupulous service, made him collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and examiner in the Secretariat household bureau, transferred him to the penal bureau, and promoted him to direct historian and National History compiler.

sentences.zh: 大理治相州獄，詳斷官竇革以白奉世，奉世曰：「君自以法從事，毋庸白。」

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review tried the Xiangzhou case; the sentencing officer Dou Ge informed Fengshi, and Fengshi said: "Sir, apply the law as you see fit—there is no need to inform me."
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review tried the Xiangzhou case. The sentencing officer Dou Ge reported to Fengshi, who said, "Apply the law as you see fit—do not report to me."

sentences.zh: 後蔡確以是文致奉世罪，謫降蔡州糧料院。

translations.literal: Later Cai Que used this to frame charges against Fengshi, and he was demoted to the Caizhou grain depot.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cai Que used this to frame him, and he was demoted to the Caizhou grain depot.

sentences.zh: 久之，爲吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he became vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he became vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，歷度支左司郎中、起居郎、天章閣待制、樞密都承旨、戶部吏部侍郎、權戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era he successively served as left-section director in the Revenue Bureau, attendance gentleman, academician on call in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation, chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, vice ministers of Revenue and Personnel, and acting minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanyou era he rose through left-section director in the Revenue Bureau, attendance gentleman, academician on call in the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation, chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, vice ministers of Revenue and Personnel, and acting minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜樞密直學士，簽書院事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed direct academician in the Bureau of Military Affairs and signed documents for the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made direct academician in the Bureau of Military Affairs with authority to sign its documents.

sentences.zh: 哲宗親政，用二內侍爲押班，中書舍人呂希純封還之。

translations.literal: When Zhezong took personal rule, two inner attendants were appointed as escort officers of the guard; Secretariat Drafter Lü Xichun sealed and returned the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong took personal rule, two inner attendants were named escort officers of the guard. Secretariat Drafter Lü Xichun sealed the commission and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 帝謂有近例，奉世曰：「雖有近例，奈人不可戶曉，顧以率先施行爲非耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said there was a recent precedent; Fengshi said: "Though there is a recent precedent, how can the people be made to understand it household by household? It is only that taking the lead in carrying it out is wrong."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cited a recent precedent. Fengshi said, "There may be a recent precedent, but the people cannot be taught it household by household. The fault lies in rushing to put it into practice first."

sentences.zh: 帝爲反命。

translations.literal: The emperor reversed the order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rescinded the order.

sentences.zh: 既而章惇當國，奉世乞免去。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Dun held power, and Fengshi begged to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhang Dun came to power, and Fengshi asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年，以端明殿學士知成德軍，改定州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaosheng he was made academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and prefect of Chengde, then transferred to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaosheng he was made academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity and prefect of Chengde, then transferred to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，知成都府。

translations.literal: After a year he was made prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 過都入覲，欲述朋黨傾邪之狀。

translations.literal: Passing through the capital to present himself, he wished to set forth how factionalists had overturned the upright.
translations.idiomatic: On his way through the capital to present himself, he wished to describe how factionalists had overturned the upright.

sentences.zh: 帝將聽其來，曾布曰：「元祐變先朝法，無一當者，奉世有力焉，最爲漏網，恐不足見。」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to hear him, but Zeng Bu said: "In Yuanyou they altered the laws of the former court without a single point that held—Fengshi had great force in this and was the chief fish that slipped the net; I fear he is not worth an audience."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was ready to hear him when Zeng Bu said, "In Yuanyou they overturned the former court's laws without a single provision that stood. Fengshi had great force in that and was the chief fish that slipped the net. I fear he is not worth an audience."

sentences.zh: 遂不許。

translations.literal: He was therefore not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore denied.

sentences.zh: 明年，責光祿少卿，分司南京，居郴州。

translations.literal: The next year he was demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments with duty at Nanjing, residing at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments with duty at Nanjing and made to reside at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞邢恕劾奉世合劉摯傾害大臣，附呂大防、蘇轍，遂登政府，再貶隰州團練副使。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor-in-Chief Xing Shu impeached Fengshi for joining Liu Zhi in harming great ministers and attaching himself to Lü Dafang and Su Zhe, thereby reaching the government, and he was again demoted to military vice commissioner of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor-in-Chief Xing Shu impeached Fengshi for joining Liu Zhi in harming great ministers and siding with Lü Dafang and Su Zhe to reach the government. He was again demoted to military vice commissioner of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，盡還其官職，知定州、大名府、鄆州。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne, all his offices were restored; he governed Dingzhou, Daming prefecture, and Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, all his offices were restored. He governed Dingzhou, Daming, and Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，再奪職，責居沂、袞，以赦得歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning his offices were again stripped; he was demoted to reside at Yi and Yan, and through an amnesty was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Chongning his offices were stripped again; he was sent to reside at Yi and Yan, and through an amnesty was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，復端明殿學士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe his title of academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenghe his title of academician of the Hall of Brilliant Clarity was restored.

sentences.zh: 薨，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 奉世優於吏治，尚安靜，文詞雅贍，最精《漢書》學。

translations.literal: Fengshi excelled in administration, prized quiet, and his literary words were elegant and ample; he was most expert in the learning of the 《Book of Han》.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshi excelled in administration, prized quiet, and wrote with elegant fullness; he was most expert in Han studies.

sentences.zh: 常云：「家世惟知事君，內省不愧，怍士大夫公論而已。

translations.literal: He often said: "Our house has only known serving the ruler; inwardly I have no shame, and I am only troubled by the public judgment of scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "Our house has only known how to serve the ruler. Inwardly I have no shame; I am troubled only by what scholar-officials say in public.

sentences.zh: 得喪，常理也，譬如寒暑加人，雖善攝生者不能無病，正須安以處之。」

translations.literal: Gain and loss are constant principle, like cold and heat added to a man—even one skilled at preserving life cannot be without illness; one must simply settle oneself to bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Gain and loss are the constant way, like cold and heat laid on a man. Even one skilled at preserving life cannot escape illness. One must simply settle oneself and bear it."

sentences.zh: 曾鞏，字子固，建昌南豐人。

translations.literal: Zeng Gong, courtesy name Zigong, was a native of Nanfeng in Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gong, courtesy name Zigong, was a native of Nanfeng in Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 生而警敏，讀書數百言，脫口輒誦。

translations.literal: From birth he was keen and quick; reading several hundred words, he could recite them as soon as they left his lips.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was keen and quick. Give him several hundred words and he could recite them the moment they left his lips.

sentences.zh: 年十二，試作《六論》，援筆而成，辭甚偉。

translations.literal: At twelve he trial-composed the 《Six Discourses》; taking up the brush he finished at once, and the language was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he trial-composed the 《Six Discourses》. He took up the brush and finished at once, and the prose was very grand.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，名聞四方。

translations.literal: Just upon reaching manhood his name was known in the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Just upon reaching manhood his name rang through the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 歐陽修見其文，奇之。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xiu saw his writing and marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xiu read his writing and marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 中嘉祐二年進士第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiayou he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調太平州司法參軍，召編校史館書籍，遷館閣校勘、集賢校理，爲實錄檢討官。

translations.literal: He was assigned judicial aide of Taiping prefecture, summoned to collate books in the History Office, promoted to archive collator and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and made examiner of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted judicial aide of Taiping prefecture, summoned to collate books in the History Office, promoted to archive collator and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and made examiner of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 出通判越州，州舊取酒場錢給募牙前，錢不足，賦諸鄉戶，期七年止；

translations.literal: He went out as assistant prefect of Yuezhou; the prefecture had long taken wine-works money to pay yamen runners, and when the money was insufficient it levied the rural households for a term of seven years;
translations.idiomatic: He went out as assistant prefect of Yuezhou. The prefecture had long taken wine-works revenue to pay yamen runners; when the funds fell short it levied rural households for a term of seven years;

sentences.zh: 期盡，募者志於多入，猶責賦如初。

translations.literal: when the term ended, the hired men aimed at greater intake and still exacted levies as at first.
translations.idiomatic: when the term ended the hired men, eager for greater intake, still exacted levies as at first.

sentences.zh: 鞏訪得其狀，立罷之。

translations.literal: Gong investigated the situation and at once abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Gong investigated and at once abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，度常平不足贍，而田野之民，不能皆至城邑。

translations.literal: In a year of famine the Ever-Normal Granary stores were insufficient to provide relief, and the people of the countryside could not all reach the towns.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine the Ever-Normal Granary could not supply enough relief, and country people could not all reach the towns.

sentences.zh: 諭告屬縣，諷富人自實粟，總十五萬石，視常平價稍增以予民。

translations.literal: He issued instructions to the subordinate counties, urging the wealthy to declare their grain themselves; in all a hundred and fifty thousand piculs were gathered, and it was sold to the people at a price slightly above the Ever-Normal rate.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the subordinate counties to urge the wealthy to declare their grain. In all a hundred and fifty thousand piculs were gathered and sold to the people at a price slightly above the Ever-Normal rate.

sentences.zh: 民得從便受粟，不出田里，而食有餘。

translations.literal: The people could receive grain conveniently; they did not leave their fields and hamlets, yet had food to spare.
translations.idiomatic: The people could take grain where they stood, never leaving field or hamlet, yet had food to spare.

sentences.zh: 又貸之種糧，使隨秋賦以償，農事不乏。

translations.literal: He also lent them seed grain to be repaid with the autumn tax, and agricultural work was not interrupted.
translations.idiomatic: He also lent seed grain to be repaid with the autumn tax, so farming did not fail.

sentences.zh: 知齊州，其治以疾奸急盜爲本。

translations.literal: As prefect of Qizhou, his governance took rooting out hidden evil and pressing hard on bandits as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Qizhou he rooted his governance in rooting out hidden evil and pressing hard on bandits.

sentences.zh: 曲堤周氏擁貲雄里中，子高橫縱，賊良民，汙婦女，服器上僭，力能動權豪，州縣吏莫敢詰，鞏取置於法。

translations.literal: The Zhou clan of Qudi held wealth and dominated the village; their son Gao ran riot, robbed good people, defiled women, and used vessels above his rank; his power could move the powerful and great families, and prefectural and county clerks did not dare inquire—Gong seized him and placed him within the law.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou clan of Qudi held wealth and dominated the countryside. Their son Gao ran riot, robbed honest folk, violated women, and used vessels above his station. His power could sway the great families, and prefectural and county clerks dared not touch him. Gong seized him and brought him under the law.

sentences.zh: 章邱民聚黨村落間，號「霸王社」，椎剽奪囚，無不如志。

translations.literal: The people of Zhangqiu gathered in clans among the villages, calling themselves the Overlord Society; they robbed and plundered and seized prisoners, and none could withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangqiu the people gathered in village clans calling themselves the Overlord Society. They robbed, plundered, and seized prisoners, and none could withstand them.

sentences.zh: 鞏配三十一人，又屬民爲保伍，使幾察其出入，有盜則鳴鼓相援，每發輒得盜。

translations.literal: Gong matched thirty-one men, and also organized the people into mutual-security groups to watch comings and goings; when there was theft they beat drums to aid one another, and each time they struck they caught the thief.
translations.idiomatic: Gong indicted thirty-one men and organized the people into mutual-security groups to watch comings and goings. At theft they beat drums to aid one another, and each alarm ended in capture.

sentences.zh: 有葛友者，名在捕中，一日，自出首。

translations.literal: There was one Ge You, whose name was on the wanted list; one day he came forward and surrendered himself.
translations.idiomatic: One Ge You, whose name was on the wanted list, one day came forward and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 鞏飲食冠裳之，假以騎從，輦所購金帛隨之，誇徇四境。

translations.literal: Gong feasted him, clothed him in cap and gown, lent him mounted attendants, and had the gold and silks purchased for him carried after in a carriage, parading through the four districts.
translations.idiomatic: Gong feasted him, dressed him in cap and gown, lent him mounted attendants, and had the gold and silks bought for him carried in a carriage through the four districts as a public show.

sentences.zh: 盜聞，多出自首。

translations.literal: When bandits heard, many came forward to surrender themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits heard, many came forward to surrender.

sentences.zh: 鞏外視章顯，實欲攜貳其徒，使之不能復合也。

translations.literal: Gong outwardly honored Zhang Xian, but in fact wished to divide his followers and make them unable to reunite.
translations.idiomatic: Gong outwardly honored Zhang Xian, but in fact meant to divide his followers so they could not reunite.

sentences.zh: 自是外戶不閉。

translations.literal: From then on outer gates were not closed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on outer gates stood unbarred.

sentences.zh: 河北發民浚河，調及它路，齊當給夫二萬。

translations.literal: Hebei drafted the people to dredge rivers, and the levy reached other circuits; Qi was to supply twenty thousand laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei drafted the people to dredge rivers, and the levy reached other circuits. Qi was to supply twenty thousand laborers.

sentences.zh: 縣初按籍三丁出夫一，鞏括其隱漏，至於九而取一，省費數倍。

translations.literal: The counties at first followed the register, one laborer from every three adult males; Gong searched out concealment and leakage until it was one from nine, saving several times the expense.
translations.idiomatic: The counties at first took one laborer from every three adult males on the register. Gong searched out concealment until the ratio was one in nine, saving several times the cost.

sentences.zh: 又弛無名渡錢，為橋以濟往來。

translations.literal: He also abolished unlisted ferry fees and built bridges to aid travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He also abolished unlisted ferry fees and built bridges for travelers.

sentences.zh: 徙傳舍，自長清抵博州，以達於魏，凡省六驛，人皆以爲利。

translations.literal: He moved relay stations from Changqing to Bozhou to reach Wei; in all six stations were cut, and people all regarded it as a benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted relay stations from Changqing to Bozhou to reach Wei. In all six stations were cut, and people everywhere counted it a gain.

sentences.zh: 徙襄州、洪州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xiangzhou and Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xiangzhou and Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 會江西歲大疫，鞏命縣鎮亭傳，悉儲藥待求，軍民不能自養者，來食息官舍，資其食飲衣襟之具，分醫視診，書其全失、多寡爲殿最。

translations.literal: It happened that Jiangxi suffered great pestilence that year; Gong ordered county and market pavilions and relay lodges all to store medicine awaiting requests. Soldiers and people who could not support themselves came to eat and lodge in government buildings; he supplied food, drink, clothing, and bedding, assigned physicians to examine and treat them, and recorded recovery, loss, and numbers for ranking.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jiangxi suffered a great pestilence. Gong ordered county and market pavilions and relay lodges to store medicine against every request. Soldiers and people who could not support themselves came to eat and lodge in government buildings; he supplied food, drink, clothing, and bedding, assigned physicians to treat them, and recorded recovery, loss, and numbers for ranking.

sentences.zh: 師征安南，所過州爲萬人備。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Annan, every prefecture it passed was to prepare for ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When the army campaigned against Annan, every prefecture it passed was told to prepare for ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 他吏暴誅亟斂，民不堪。

translations.literal: Other officials violently exacted and urgently levied, and the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Other officials exacted with violence and levied in haste, and the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 鞏先期區處猝集，師去，市里不知。

translations.literal: Gong made arrangements beforehand for sudden gatherings; when the army left, the markets and lanes did not know it.
translations.idiomatic: Gong arranged beforehand for sudden gatherings. When the army left, markets and lanes scarcely knew it had passed.

sentences.zh: 加直龍圖閣、知福州。

translations.literal: He was given the added title of direct academician in the Hall of Dragon Pictures and made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added title of direct academician in the Hall of Dragon Pictures and made prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 南劍將樂盜廖恩既赦罪出降，餘眾潰復合，陰相結附，旁連數州，尤桀者呼之不至，居人懾恐。

translations.literal: In Nanjian, the bandit Liao En of Jiangle, though pardoned and released from punishment, had scattered remnants who reunited in secret, linking several prefectures beside them; the most violent would not come when called, and residents lived in fear.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanjian the Jiangle bandit Liao En, though pardoned and released, had scattered remnants who reunited in secret and linked several neighboring prefectures. The most violent would not come when summoned, and residents lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 鞏以計羅致之，繼自歸者二百輩。

translations.literal: Gong by stratagem brought them in; those who thereafter surrendered of themselves numbered two hundred parties.
translations.idiomatic: Gong by stratagem drew them in; two hundred parties thereafter surrendered of themselves.

sentences.zh: 福多佛寺，僧利其富饒，爭欲爲主守，賕請公行。

translations.literal: Fu had many Buddhist temples; monks coveted their wealth and contended to become chief guardians, bribing and pleading openly.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou had many Buddhist temples. Monks coveted their wealth and fought to become chief guardians, bribing and pleading openly.

sentences.zh: 鞏俾其徒相推擇，識諸籍，以次補之。

translations.literal: Gong had their disciples choose among themselves, recorded them in registers, and filled posts in order.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had their disciples choose among themselves, entered them in registers, and filled posts in order.

sentences.zh: 授帖於府庭，卻其私謝，以絕左右徼求之弊。

translations.literal: He issued the commission in the prefectural court and refused private thanks, thereby cutting off the evil of importunate requests from those about him.
translations.idiomatic: He issued commissions in the prefectural court and refused private thanks, cutting off the evil of importunate requests from those about him.

sentences.zh: 福州無職田，歲鬻園蔬收其直，自入常三四十萬。

translations.literal: Fuzhou had no official fields; each year it sold garden vegetables and took in three or four hundred thousand in cash for the prefect himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou had no official fields. Each year it sold garden vegetables and took in three or four hundred thousand in cash for the prefect's own purse.

sentences.zh: 鞏曰：「太守與民爭利，可乎？」

translations.literal: Gong said: "Is it fitting for a prefect to contend with the people for profit?"
translations.idiomatic: Gong said, "Is it fitting for a prefect to contend with the people for profit?"

sentences.zh: 罷之。

translations.literal: He abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 後至者亦不復取也。

translations.literal: Those who came after also did not take it again.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came after did not take it up again either.

sentences.zh: 徙明、亳、滄三州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Ming, Bo, and Cang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Mingzhou, Bozhou, and Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鞏負才名，久外徒，世頗謂偃蹇不偶。

translations.literal: Gong bore a reputation for talent; long transferred outward, the age largely thought him proud and ill-matched to his times.
translations.idiomatic: Gong bore a reputation for talent. Long posted outside the capital, the age largely thought him proud and ill-matched to fortune.

sentences.zh: 一時後生輩鋒出，鞏視之泊如也。

translations.literal: A generation of younger men suddenly rose sharp; Gong looked on them with calm detachment.
translations.idiomatic: A generation of younger men rose sharp all at once; Gong looked on them with calm detachment.

sentences.zh: 過闕，神宗召見，勞問甚寵，遂留判三班院。

translations.literal: Passing the capital, Shenzong summoned him, questioned him with great favor, and kept him to judge the Three-Rank Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the capital, Shenzong summoned him, questioned him with great favor, and kept him to judge the Three-Rank Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上疏議經費，帝曰：「鞏以節用爲理財之要，世之言理財者，未有及此。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on state expenditure; the emperor said: "Gong takes frugality as the key to managing finances; among those who speak of managing finances, none has reached this."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on state expenditure. The emperor said, "Gong takes frugality as the key to managing finances. Among those who speak of managing finances, none has reached this."

sentences.zh: 帝以《三朝》、《兩朝國史》各自爲書，將合而爲一，加鞏史館修撰，專典之，不以大臣監總，既而不克成。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the 《Histories of Three Reigns》 and the 《History of Two Reigns》 each stood as separate books, wished to combine them into one; he added Gong as reviser in the History Office with sole charge of the work, not placing it under supervision by a great minister—and in the end it could not be completed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because the 《Histories of Three Reigns》 and the 《History of Two Reigns》 each stood as separate works, wished to combine them into one. He made Gong reviser in the History Office with sole charge of the compilation, without placing a great minister over it—and in the end the project could not be completed.

sentences.zh: 會官制行，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When the official system reform was carried out, he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When the new bureaucratic system took effect, he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時自三省百職事，選授一新，除書日至十數，人人舉其職，於訓辭典約而盡。

translations.literal: At that time, from the Three Departments down through the hundred offices, selection and appointment were wholly renewed; dismissal and appointment documents arrived by the dozen each day; every man performed his office; in edicts and instructions he was concise and exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: Selection and appointment throughout the Three Departments and the hundred offices were wholly renewed. Dismissal and appointment orders arrived by the dozen each day, and every man performed his duty. In edicts and instructions he was concise yet complete.

sentences.zh: 尋掌延安郡王牒奏。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter he took charge of memorials and reports for the Prince of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of memorials and reports for the Prince of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 故事命翰林學士，至是特屬之。

translations.literal: By precedent a Hanlin Academician was appointed; on this occasion it was specially assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent a Hanlin Academician had held the post; on this occasion it was specially entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 甫數月，丁母艱去。

translations.literal: Only a few months later he left on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few months later he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 又數月而卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: A few months later he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he died, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 鞏性孝友，父亡，奉繼母益至，撫四弟、九妹於委廢單弱之中，宦學昏嫁，一出其力。

translations.literal: Gong was by nature filial and brotherly. After his father's death he served his stepmother with utmost devotion and raised four younger brothers and nine younger sisters amid ruin and helpless weakness—official careers, schooling, and marriages all at his expense.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was by nature filial and devoted to his kin. After his father's death he served his stepmother with utmost care and, amid ruin and helpless weakness, raised four younger brothers and nine younger sisters—official careers, schooling, and marriages alike at his own expense.

sentences.zh: 爲文章，上下馳騁，愈出而愈工，本原《六經》，斟酌於司馬遷、韓愈，一時工作文詞者，鮮能過也。

translations.literal: In composing essays he ranged freely up and down; the more he produced the more refined his work became. He took the 《Six Classics》 as his root and drew on Sima Qian and Han Yu; among contemporary masters of literary composition few could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: In his writing he ranged freely up and down; the more he wrote, the more refined his work grew. He took the 《Six Classics》 as his foundation and drew on Sima Qian and Han Yu. Among the masters of literary composition of his day, few could surpass him.

sentences.zh: 少與王安石游，安石聲譽未振，鞏導之於歐陽修，及安石得志，遂與之異。

translations.literal: In youth he associated with Wang Anshi. Before Anshi's reputation had risen, Gong introduced him to Ouyang Xiu. Once Anshi gained power, Gong parted from him.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he associated with Wang Anshi. Before Anshi's reputation had risen, Gong introduced him to Ouyang Xiu. Once Anshi gained power, Gong broke with him.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗問：「安石何如人？」

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong once asked, "What sort of man is Anshi?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong once asked, "What sort of man is Anshi?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「安石文學行義，不減揚雄，以吝故不及。」

translations.literal: He replied, "In learning and conduct Anshi does not fall short of Yang Xiong, but because of stinginess he does not measure up.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In learning and conduct Anshi does not fall short of Yang Xiong, yet because of stinginess he does not measure up."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「安石輕富貴，何吝也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Anshi holds wealth and rank lightly—how is he stingy?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Anshi holds wealth and rank lightly. How is he stingy?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣所謂吝者，謂其勇於有爲，吝於改過耳。」

translations.literal: He said, "What your servant means by stinginess is that he is bold in acting yet stingy in correcting his errors.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "What your servant means by stinginess is that he is bold in acting yet reluctant to amend his faults."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 呂公著嘗告神宗，以鞏爲人行義不如政事，政事不如文章，以是不大用云。

translations.literal: Lü Gongzhu once told Shenzong that in conduct and righteousness Gong fell short of his administration, and his administration fell short of his writing—therefore he was not greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongzhu once told Shenzong that Gong's conduct and righteousness were inferior to his administration, and his administration inferior to his writing. For this reason he was not greatly employed.

sentences.zh: 弟:布，自有傳、幼弟：肇。

translations.literal: Younger brother Bu has his own biography; youngest brother Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Bu has his own biography; his youngest brother was Zhao.

sentences.zh: 弟 肇

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Zhao

sentences.zh: 弟肇，字子開，舉進士，調黃岩簿，用薦爲鄭州教授，擢崇文校書、館閣校勘兼國子監直講、同知太常禮院。

translations.literal: Zhao, styled Zikai, passed the civil service examination, was appointed recorder of Huangyan, and through recommendation became instructor at Zhengzhou. He was promoted to collator of the Chongwen Library, collator in the Hall of Imperial Writings while also serving as direct lecturer in the Directorate of Education, and concurrently vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, whose courtesy name was Zikai, passed the civil service examination and was appointed recorder of Huangyan. On recommendation he became instructor at Zhengzhou, then was promoted collator of the Chongwen Library and collator in the Hall of Imperial Writings, while also serving as direct lecturer in the Directorate of Education and concurrently vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太常自秦以來，禮文殘缺，先儒各以臆說，無所稽據。

translations.literal: Since Qin the ritual texts of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had been damaged and lost; earlier scholars each offered private interpretations with nothing to verify them against.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Qin dynasty the ritual texts of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had been damaged and lost, and earlier scholars had offered private interpretations with nothing authoritative to verify them against.

sentences.zh: 肇在職，多所厘正。

translations.literal: While Zhao held office he corrected many points.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhao held office he corrected many points.

sentences.zh: 親祠皇地祗於北郊，蓋自肇發之，異論莫能奪其議。

translations.literal: The personal sacrifice to Earth at the northern suburban altar was in origin his proposal; rival opinions could not overturn his argument.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's personal sacrifice to Earth at the northern suburban altar originated with him, and rival opinions could not overturn his argument.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎韓維奏范百祿事，太皇太后以爲讒毀，出守鄧。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat Han Wei memorialized on the affair of Fan Bailu. The Grand Empress Dowager regarded it as slander and had him sent out to guard Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Secretariat Han Wei memorialized on the affair of Fan Bailu. The Grand Empress Dowager regarded it as slander and had him sent out to guard Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 肇言：「維爲朝廷辨邪正是非，不可以疑似逐。」

translations.literal: Zhao said, "Wei was distinguishing right from wrong for the court on behalf of the throne; he must not be dismissed on mere suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Wei was distinguishing right from wrong for the court on behalf of the throne. He must not be dismissed on mere suspicion."

sentences.zh: 不草制。

translations.literal: He refused to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫王覿，以論胡宗愈，出守潤，肇言：「陛下寄腹心於大臣，寄耳目於臺諫，二者相須，闕一不可。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Wang Xi, for criticizing Hu Zongyu, was sent out to guard Runzhou. Zhao said, "Your Majesty entrusts his inmost thoughts to great ministers and his eyes and ears to remonstrators and censors—the two rely on each other; neither can be dispensed with.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Censor Wang Xi, for criticizing Hu Zongyu, was sent out to guard Runzhou. Zhao said, "Your Majesty entrusts his inmost thoughts to great ministers and his eyes and ears to remonstrators and censors. The two rely on each other, and neither can be dispensed with.

sentences.zh: 今覿論執政即去之，是愛腹心而塗耳目也。」

translations.literal: Now Xi is dismissed for criticizing the chief minister—that is to cherish the inmost heart while blinding the eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xi is dismissed for criticizing the chief minister. That is to cherish the inmost heart while blinding the eyes and ears."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，加覿直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: The Emperor understood and added Xi to the directorship of the Hall of Dragon Pictures.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took his meaning and added Xi to the directorship of the Hall of Dragon Pictures.

sentences.zh: 太皇受冊，詔遵章獻故事，御文德殿。

translations.literal: When the Grand Empress Dowager received her investiture, an edict followed the Zhang Xian precedent and she was to attend at the Hall of Literary Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Empress Dowager received her investiture, an edict followed the Zhang Xian precedent and she was to attend at the Hall of Literary Virtue.

sentences.zh: 肇言：「天聖初，兩制定議受冊崇政，仁宗特改焉，此蓋一時之制。

translations.literal: Zhao said, "At the beginning of the Tiansheng era the two systems had agreed that investiture should be received at Chongzheng; Emperor Renzong specially changed it—this was a measure for a particular time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "At the beginning of the Tiansheng era the two systems had agreed that investiture should be received at Chongzheng. Emperor Renzong specially changed it. This was a measure for a particular time.

sentences.zh: 今帝述仁宗故事，以極崇奉孝敬之誠，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: Now the Emperor follows Renzong's precedent to the utmost in honoring filial devotion—this may be called perfect.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Emperor follows Renzong's precedent to the utmost in honoring filial devotion. This may be called perfect.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂太皇當於此時特下詔揚帝孝敬之誠，而固執謙德，屈從天聖兩制之議，止於崇政，則帝孝愈顯，太皇之德愈尊矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to think that at this time the Grand Empress Dowager should specially issue an edict praising the Emperor's filial devotion, yet firmly hold to modest virtue and yield to the Tiansheng two-systems proposal, stopping at Chongzheng—then the Emperor's filial piety would shine the brighter and the Grand Empress Dowager's virtue would stand the higher.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant ventures to think that at this time the Grand Empress Dowager should specially issue an edict praising the Emperor's filial devotion, yet firmly hold to modest virtue and yield to the Tiansheng two-systems proposal, stopping at Chongzheng. Then the Emperor's filial piety would shine the brighter and the Grand Empress Dowager's virtue would stand the higher."

sentences.zh: 坤成節上壽，議令百官班崇政。

translations.literal: On the Kuncheng Festival when longevity was offered, it was debated whether officials should line up at Chongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the Kuncheng Festival, when longevity was offered, it was debated whether officials should line up at Chongzheng.

sentences.zh: 肇又言：「天聖三年，近臣班殿廷，百官止請內東門拜表。

translations.literal: Zhao again said, "In the third year of Tiansheng, close attendants lined up in the palace hall; the hundred officials only submitted congratulatory memorials at the inner east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao again said, "In the third year of Tiansheng, close attendants lined up in the palace hall, while the hundred officials only submitted congratulatory memorials at the inner east gate.

sentences.zh: 至九年，始御會慶。

translations.literal: Not until the ninth year did he first attend at Huiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the ninth year did he first attend at Huiqing.

sentences.zh: 今太皇盛德，不肯自同章獻，宜如三年之制。」

translations.literal: Now the Grand Empress Dowager's virtue is so great that she is unwilling to equate herself with Zhang Xian; it is fitting to follow the third-year system.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Empress Dowager's virtue is so great that she is unwilling to equate herself with Zhang Xian. It is fitting to follow the third-year system."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: Both were followed.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 四年，春旱，有司猶講春宴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year spring drought struck; the relevant offices still planned the spring banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year a spring drought struck, yet the relevant offices still planned the spring banquet.

sentences.zh: 肇同彭汝礪上疏曰：「天菑方作，正君臣側身畏懼之時。

translations.literal: Zhao together with Peng Ruli submitted a memorial saying, "Heaven's calamity has just begun—this is precisely the time for ruler and ministers to restrain themselves in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao together with Peng Ruli submitted a memorial saying, "Heaven's calamity has just begun. This is precisely the time for ruler and ministers to restrain themselves in fear.

sentences.zh: 乃相與飲食燕樂，恐無以消復天變。」

translations.literal: Yet you gather to drink, feast, and make merry— I fear there will be no way to dispel and restore Heaven's change.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you gather to drink, feast, and make merry. I fear there will be no way to dispel Heaven's wrath and restore order."

sentences.zh: 翼日，有旨罷宴。

translations.literal: The next day there was an order canceling the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an order canceled the banquet.

sentences.zh: 蔡確貶新州，肇先與汝礪相約極論。

translations.literal: Cai Que was demoted to Xinzhou. Zhao had earlier agreed with Ruli to argue to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que was demoted to Xinzhou. Zhao had earlier agreed with Ruli to argue the matter to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 會除給事中，汝礪獨封還制書，言者謂肇賣友，略不自辨。

translations.literal: When he was appointed Supervising Secretary, Ruli alone sealed and returned the edict. Critics said Zhao had betrayed his friend; he scarcely defended himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed Supervising Secretary, Ruli alone sealed and returned the edict. Critics said Zhao had betrayed his friend, yet he scarcely defended himself.

sentences.zh: 以寶文閣待制知潁州，徙鄧、齊、陳州、應天府。

translations.literal: As a pending appointee of the Hall of Literary Treasures he was made prefect of Yingzhou, then transferred to Deng, Qi, Chen, and Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: As a pending appointee of the Hall of Literary Treasures he was made prefect of Yingzhou, then transferred to Deng, Qi, Chen, and Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 七年，入爲吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 肇在禮院時，啟親祠北郊之議。

translations.literal: When Zhao was at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he had opened the debate on personally sacrificing at the northern suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he had opened the debate on the emperor's personal sacrifice at the northern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 是歲當郊，肇堅抗前說，既而合祭天地，乃自劾，改刑部。

translations.literal: That year the suburban sacrifice was due; Zhao firmly resisted his earlier view. When Heaven and Earth were thereafter sacrificed together, he impeached himself and was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: That year the suburban sacrifice was due. Zhao firmly held to his earlier view, but when Heaven and Earth were thereafter sacrificed together, he impeached himself and was transferred to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 請不已，出知徐州，徙江寧府。

translations.literal: He pleaded without cease and was sent out as prefect of Xuzhou, then transferred to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded without cease and was sent out as prefect of Xuzhou, then transferred to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 帝親政，更用舊臣，數稱肇議禮，趣入對。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took personal rule he again employed old ministers and several times praised Zhao's ritual arguments, urging him to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took personal rule he again employed old ministers and several times praised Zhao's ritual arguments, urging him to an audience.

sentences.zh: 肇言：「人主雖有自然之聖質，必賴左右前後得人，以爲立政之本。

translations.literal: Zhao said, "Though the sovereign by nature possesses innate sagely quality, he must rely on those about him left and right, before and behind, gaining the right men to serve as the foundation of government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said, "Though the sovereign by nature possesses innate sagely quality, he must rely on those about him—left and right, before and behind—gaining the right men to serve as the foundation of government.

sentences.zh: 宜於此時選忠信端良之士，置諸近班，以參謀議，備顧問。
