translations.literal: At this time he should select men loyal, trustworthy, upright, and good and place them in the near ranks to deliberate on policy and stand ready for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he should select men who are loyal, trustworthy, upright, and good and place them in the near ranks to deliberate on policy and stand ready for consultation.

sentences.zh: 與夫深處法宮，親近暬御，其損益相去萬萬矣。」

translations.literal: Compared with dwelling deep in the law palace and drawing close to intimate attendants, the gain and loss are separated by ten thousandfold.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with dwelling deep in the law palace and drawing close only to intimate attendants, the gain and loss are separated by ten thousandfold."

sentences.zh: 貴近惡其語，出知瀛州，與兄布易地。

translations.literal: The powerful and near hated his words; he was sent out as prefect of Yingzhou and exchanged posts with his elder brother Bu.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful and those close to the throne hated his words. He was sent out as prefect of Yingzhou and exchanged posts with his elder brother Bu.

sentences.zh: 時方治實錄譏訕罪，降爲滁州。

translations.literal: At that time the Veritable Records slander case was being prosecuted; he was demoted to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Veritable Records slander case was being prosecuted, and he was demoted to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 稍復集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored as compiler of the Hall for Collecting Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as compiler of the Hall for Collecting Worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷泰州、海州。

translations.literal: He served in succession at Taizhou and Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession at Taizhou and Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗即位，復召爲中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Huizong took the throne Zhao was again summoned as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong took the throne, Zhao was again summoned as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 日食四月朔，當降詔求言。

translations.literal: An eclipse fell on the first day of the fourth month; an edict seeking remonstrance ought to be issued.
translations.idiomatic: An eclipse fell on the first day of the fourth month. An edict seeking remonstrance ought to be issued.

sentences.zh: 肇具述帝旨，詔下，投匭者如織。

translations.literal: Zhao fully set forth the Emperor's intent; when the edict was issued, submissions poured in like woven silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao fully set forth the Emperor's intent. When the edict was issued, submissions poured in like woven silk.

sentences.zh: 章惇惡之，欲因事去肇，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun hated this and wished to remove Zhao on some pretext; the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun hated this and wished to remove Zhao on some pretext, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 元祐臣僚被譴者，咸以赦恩甄敘。

translations.literal: Yuan You officials who had been punished all received amnesty and restoration of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan You officials who had been punished all received amnesty and restoration of rank.

sentences.zh: 肇請併錄死者，作訓詞，哀厚惻怛，讀者爲之感愴。

translations.literal: Zhao requested that the dead also be recorded together and a training edict drafted—so mournful and thick with compassion that readers were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao requested that the dead also be recorded together and a training edict drafted, so mournful and thick with compassion that readers were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician while also serving as Lector.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician while also serving as Lector.

sentences.zh: 諫官陳瓘、給事中龔原以言得罪，無敢救，肇極力論解。

translations.literal: Remonstrator Chen Guan and Supervising Secretary Gong Yuan were punished for their words; none dared rescue them, but Zhao argued strenuously on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrator Chen Guan and Supervising Secretary Gong Yuan were punished for their words. None dared rescue them, but Zhao argued strenuously on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 時論者謂元祐、紹聖，均為有失，兄布傳帝命，使肇作詔諭天下。

translations.literal: Contemporary critics held that both Yuan You and Shao Sheng had erred; the elder brother Bu transmitted the Emperor's command that Zhao draft an edict to instruct the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary critics held that both Yuan You and Shao Sheng had erred. The elder brother Bu transmitted the Emperor's command that Zhao draft an edict to instruct the realm.

sentences.zh: 肇見帝言：「陛下思建皇極，以消弭朋黨，須先分別君子小人，賞善罰惡，不可偏廢。」

translations.literal: Zhao saw the Emperor and said, "Your Majesty wishes to establish the imperial norm and dissolve faction, but must first distinguish gentlemen from petty men and reward good and punish evil without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao saw the Emperor and said, "Your Majesty wishes to establish the imperial norm and dissolve faction, but must first distinguish gentlemen from petty men and reward good and punish evil without partiality."

sentences.zh: 開說備至。

translations.literal: He expounded this at full length.
translations.idiomatic: He expounded this at full length.

sentences.zh: 已而詔從中出。

translations.literal: Before long the edict issued from the center.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the edict issued from the center.

sentences.zh: 布之拜相，肇適當制，國朝學士弟草兄制，惟韓維與肇，為衣冠榮。

translations.literal: When Bu received the seal of chief minister, Zhao happened to draft the appointment; in the dynasty a younger brother drafting his elder brother's appointment had occurred only with Han Wei and Zhao—a glory for the scholar-official class.
translations.idiomatic: When Bu received the seal of chief minister, Zhao happened to draft the appointment. In the dynasty a younger brother drafting his elder brother's appointment had occurred only with Han Wei and Zhao—a glory for the scholar-official class.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，太史奏日又當食四月。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo the Grand Astrologer reported that the sun would again be eclipsed in the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong Jingguo the Grand Astrologer reported that the sun would again be eclipsed in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 肇請對言：「比歲日食正陽，咎異章著。

translations.literal: Zhao requested an audience and said, "In recent years the sun was eclipsed at the yang zenith; omens and anomalies were plain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao requested an audience and said, "In recent years the sun was eclipsed at the yang zenith, and omens and anomalies were plain.

sentences.zh: 陛下簡儉清淨之化，或衰於前；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's frugal and pure governance may have waned from before;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's frugal and pure governance may have waned from before;

sentences.zh: 聲色服玩之好，或萌於心；

translations.literal: delight in sound, color, dress, and playthings may have sprouted in the heart;
translations.idiomatic: delight in sound, color, dress, and playthings may have sprouted in the heart;

sentences.zh: 忠邪賢不肖，或有未辨；

translations.literal: the loyal and the treacherous, the worthy and the unworthy, may still be undistinguished;
translations.idiomatic: the loyal and the treacherous, the worthy and the unworthy, may still be undistinguished;

sentences.zh: 賞慶刑威，或有未當。

translations.literal: rewards, celebrations, punishments, and authority may still be in error.
translations.idiomatic: rewards, celebrations, punishments, and authority may still be in error.

sentences.zh: 左右阿諛，壅蔽矯舉，民冤失職，鬱不得伸。

translations.literal: Flatterers left and right block and distort reports; the people's grievances lose office and are pent up without redress.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers to left and right block and distort reports. The people's grievances lose office and are pent up without redress.

sentences.zh: 此宜反覆循省，痛自克責，以塞天變。」

translations.literal: At this the ruler should turn again and again to examine himself, painfully reproach himself, to stem Heaven's change.
translations.idiomatic: At this the ruler should turn again and again to examine himself and painfully reproach himself, to stem Heaven's wrath."

sentences.zh: 言發涕下，帝悚然順納。

translations.literal: As he spoke tears fell; the Emperor was startled and obediently accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke, tears fell. The Emperor was startled and obediently accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 兄布在相位，引故事避禁職，拜龍圖閣學士、提舉中太一宮。

translations.literal: The elder brother Bu held the chief minister's post and, citing precedent, avoided forbidden offices; he was appointed academician of the Hall of Dragon Pictures and put in charge of the Central Supreme Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The elder brother Bu held the chief minister's post and, citing precedent, avoided forbidden offices. He was appointed academician of the Hall of Dragon Pictures and put in charge of the Central Supreme Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出知陳州，歷太原、應天府、揚、定二州。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Chenzhou, then served in succession at Taiyuan, Yingtian, Yang, and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as prefect of Chenzhou, then served in succession at Taiyuan, Yingtian, Yang, and Ding.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，落職，謫知和州，徙岳州，繼貶濮州團練副使，安置汀州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning he was stripped of office, demoted to prefect of Hezhou, transferred to Yuezhou, then further demoted to military training vice commissioner of Puzhou and settled at Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongning he was stripped of office, demoted to prefect of Hezhou, transferred to Yuezhou, then further demoted to military training vice commissioner of Puzhou and settled at Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，歸潤而卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he returned to Run and died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned to Run and died, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧以來四十年，大臣更用事，邪正相軋，黨論屢起，肇身更其間，數不合。

translations.literal: From the Xining era for forty years great ministers succeeded one another in power; the wicked and the upright pressed against each other and factional debate rose again and again. Zhao passed through it all and several times fell out of step.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xining era for forty years great ministers succeeded one another in power. The wicked and the upright pressed against each other, and factional debate rose again and again. Zhao passed through it all and several times fell out of step.

sentences.zh: 兄布與韓忠彥並相，日夕傾危之。

translations.literal: The elder brother Bu served as chief minister together with Han Zhongyan; day and night they undermined each other.
translations.idiomatic: The elder brother Bu served as chief minister together with Han Zhongyan and day and night they undermined each other.

sentences.zh: 肇既居外，移書告之曰：「兄方得君，當引用善人，翊正道，以杜惇、卞復起之萌。

translations.literal: Once Zhao was outside office he wrote to inform him, "Elder brother has just won the ruler's trust; you should employ good men and support the correct Way to cut off the sprouting of Zhang Dun and Cai Bian's return.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao was outside office he wrote to inform him, "Elder brother has just won the ruler's trust. You should employ good men and support the correct Way to cut off the sprouting of Zhang Dun and Cai Bian's return.

sentences.zh: 而數月以來，所謂端人吉士，繼跡去朝，所進以爲輔佐、侍從、臺諫，往往皆前日事惇、卞者。

translations.literal: Yet in the months since, the so-called upright men and gentlemen of good omen have left the court one after another; those advanced as aides, attendants, and remonstrators and censors are often the very men who once served Zhang Dun and Cai Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the months since, the so-called upright men and gentlemen of good omen have left the court one after another. Those advanced as aides, attendants, and remonstrators and censors are often the very men who once served Zhang Dun and Cai Bian.

sentences.zh: 一旦勢異今日，必首引之以為固位計，思之可爲慟哭。

translations.literal: Once power shifts from today, they will surely be the first to bring them in to secure their own positions— to think of it is cause for wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Once power shifts from today, they will surely be the first to bring them in to secure their own positions. To think of it is cause for wailing.

sentences.zh: 比來主意已移，小人道長。

translations.literal: Of late the ruler's intent has already shifted; petty men grow long in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Of late the ruler's intent has already shifted, and petty men grow long in the Way.

sentences.zh: 進則必論元祐人於帝前，退則盡排元祐者於要路。

translations.literal: Advancing, they will surely discuss Yuan You men before the Emperor; retreating, they will wholly exclude Yuan You men from key posts.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing, they will surely discuss Yuan You men before the Emperor; retreating, they will wholly exclude Yuan You men from key posts.

sentences.zh: 異時惇、卞縱未至，一蔡京足以兼二人，可不深慮。」

translations.literal: In time Zhang Dun and Cai Bian may not yet arrive, but Cai Jing alone is enough to encompass the two— this must be deeply considered.
translations.idiomatic: In time Zhang Dun and Cai Bian may not yet arrive, but Cai Jing alone is enough to encompass the two. This must be deeply considered."

sentences.zh: 布不能從。

translations.literal: Bu could not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Bu could not follow him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，京得政，布與肇俱不免。

translations.literal: Before long Jing gained power and Bu and Zhao alike could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jing gained power, and Bu and Zhao alike could not escape.

sentences.zh: 肇天資仁厚，而容貌端嚴。

translations.literal: Zhao was by nature humane and generous, yet in appearance grave and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was by nature humane and generous, yet in appearance grave and stern.

sentences.zh: 自少力學，博覽經傳，爲文溫潤有法。

translations.literal: From youth he studied strenuously, reading widely in the classics and their commentaries; his writing was warm and polished and had method.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied strenuously and read widely in the classics and their commentaries. His writing was warm, polished, and methodical.

sentences.zh: 更十一州，類多善政。

translations.literal: Across eleven prefectures he mostly achieved good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Across eleven prefectures he mostly achieved good administration.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，諡曰文昭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaoxing era he was given the posthumous title Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaoxing era he was given the posthumous title Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 子統，至左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His son Tong rose to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong rose to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 論曰：劉敞博學雄文，鄰于邃古，其爲考功，仁宗賜夏竦諡，上疏爭之，以爲人主不可侵臣下之官；

translations.literal: The commentator says: Liu Chang was broadly learned with powerful writing, neighbor to the remote ancients. When he served in the Ministry of Personnel, Emperor Renzong bestowed Xia Song's posthumous title; he submitted a memorial disputing it, holding that the sovereign must not infringe an office belonging to his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Liu Chang was broadly learned, with writing of formidable power akin to the remote ancients. When he served in the Ministry of Personnel, Emperor Renzong bestowed Xia Song's posthumous title. He submitted a memorial disputing it, holding that the sovereign must not infringe an office belonging to his subjects.

sentences.zh: 及奉詔定樂，中貴預列，又諫曰：「臣懼爲袁盎所笑。」

translations.literal: When he received the edict to fix the music and palace eunuchs sat in the ranks, he again remonstrated, "Your servant fears becoming an object of Yuan Ang's laughter.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the edict to fix the music and palace eunuchs sat in the ranks, he again remonstrated, "Your servant fears becoming an object of Yuan Ang's laughter.

sentences.zh: 此豈事君為容悅者哉。

translations.literal: Is this one who serves his lord by pleasing his countenance?
translations.idiomatic: Is this one who serves his lord by pleasing his countenance?"

sentences.zh: 攽雖疏雋，文埒於敞。

translations.literal: Ban, though spare and sharp, in writing matched Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Ban, though spare and sharp, in writing matched Chang.

sentences.zh: 奉世克肖，世稱「三劉」。

translations.literal: Fengshi was his equal in likeness; the age called them "the Three Liu."
translations.idiomatic: Fengshi was his equal in likeness; the age called them "the Three Liu."

sentences.zh: 曾鞏立言于歐陽修、王安石間，紆徐而不煩，簡奧而不晦，卓然自成一家，可謂難矣。

translations.literal: Zeng Gong set forth his views between Ouyang Xiu and Wang Anshi—unhurried yet not prolix, concise and abstruse yet not obscure; standing alone as a school of his own—this may be called difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gong set forth his views between Ouyang Xiu and Wang Anshi—unhurried yet not prolix, concise and abstruse yet not obscure, standing alone as a school of his own. This may be called difficult.

sentences.zh: 肇以儒者而有能吏之才。

translations.literal: Zhao was a Confucian who yet possessed the talent of a capable administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was a Confucian who yet possessed the talent of a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 宋之中葉，文學法理，咸精其能，若劉氏、曾氏之家學，蓋有兩漢之風焉。

translations.literal: In the mid-Song, in literature, principle, and law all mastered their craft; in household learning such as the Liu and Zeng families there was something of the wind of the two Han dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-Song, in literature, principle, and law all mastered their craft. In household learning such as the Liu and Zeng families there was something of the wind of the two Han dynasties.
